14.29.s:
.. paulastya uvāca .. ..
tato gacchennṛpaśreṣṭha kapilātīrthamuttamam ..
yatra snāto naraḥ samyaṅmucyate sarvakilbiṣaiḥ .. 1 ..
14.29.d:
.. पौलस्त्य उवाच .. ..
ततो गच्छेन्नृपश्रेष्ठ कपिलातीर्थमुत्तमम् ..
यत्र स्नातो नरः सम्यङ्मुच्यते सर्वकिल्बिषैः .. 1 ..
14.29.m:
Pulastya said:
Then one should go, O best of kings, to the supreme Kapilātīrtha,
where a man, properly bathed, is freed from all sins.

14.29.s:
purā'bhūnnṛpatirnāma suprabhaḥ paravīrahā ..
nityaṃ ca mṛgayāśīlo mṛgāṇāmahite rataḥ .. 2 ..
14.29.d:
पुराऽभून्नृपतिर्नाम सुप्रभः परवीरहा ..
नित्यं च मृगयाशीलो मृगाणामहिते रतः .. 2 ..
14.29.m:
Formerly there was a king named Suprabha, a slayer of enemy heroes,
always devoted to hunting and intent on harming deer.

14.29.s:
na tathā strīṣu no bhoge nāśvayāne na vāraṇe ..
tasyābhūdanurāgaśca yathā mṛgavimarddane .. 3 ..
14.29.d:
न तथा स्त्रीषु नो भोगे नाश्वयाने न वारणे ..
तस्याभूदनुरागश्च यथा मृगविमर्द्दने .. 3 ..
14.29.m:
He did not have such passion for women, nor for pleasures, nor for riding horses or elephants,
as he had for destroying deer.

14.29.s:
sa kadācinnṛpaśreṣṭha mṛgāsakto'rbudaṃ gataḥ ..
apaśyatsānudeśe ca mṛgīṃ śiśusamāvṛtām .. 4 ..
14.29.d:
स कदाचिन्नृपश्रेष्ठ मृगासक्तोऽर्बुदं गतः ..
अपश्यत्सानुदेशे च मृगीं शिशुसमावृताम् .. 4 ..
14.29.m:
Once, O best of kings, intent on deer, he went to Arbuda.
And on a mountain slope he saw a doe surrounded by her young,

14.29.s:
stanaṃ dhayantīṃ susnigdhāṃ śiśoḥ kṣīrānurāgiṇaḥ ..
sā tena viddhā bāṇena sahasā nataparvaṇā .. 5 ..
14.29.d:
स्तनं धयन्तीं सुस्निग्धां शिशोः क्षीरानुरागिणः ..
सा तेन विद्धा बाणेन सहसा नतपर्वणा .. 5 ..
14.29.m:
very tenderly nursing her child who was fond of milk.
She was suddenly pierced by him with a bent-knotted arrow.

14.29.s:
atha sā pārthivaṃ dṛṣṭvā pragṛhītaśarāsanam ..
dvitīyaṃ yojayānaṃ ca mṛgī bāṇaṃ sunirmalam .. 6 ..
14.29.d:
अथ सा पार्थिवं दृष्ट्वा प्रगृहीतशरासनम् ..
द्वितीयं योजयानं च मृगी बाणं सुनिर्मलम् .. 6 ..
14.29.m:
Then, seeing the king holding his bow
and fitting a second bright arrow, the doe,

14.29.s:
tataḥ sā kopasantaptā bhūpālaṃ pratyabhāṣata ..
nāyaṃ dharmaḥ smṛtaḥ kṣāttro yastvayādya niṣevitaḥ ..7 ..
14.29.d:
ततः सा कोपसन्तप्ता भूपालं प्रत्यभाषत ..
नायं धर्मः स्मृतः क्षात्त्रो यस्त्वयाद्य निषेवितः ..7 ..
14.29.m:
afflicted with rage, spoke back to the king:
"This has not been declared the duty of a kṣatriya, which you have practiced today!

14.29.s:
śayāno maithunāsaktaḥ stanapo vyādhipīḍitaḥ ..
na haṃtavyo mṛgo rājanmṛgī ca śiśunā vṛtā .. 8 ..
14.29.d:
शयानो मैथुनासक्तः स्तनपो व्याधिपीडितः ..
न हंतव्यो मृगो राजन्मृगी च शिशुना वृता .. 8 ..
14.29.m:
A deer that is lying down, engaged in mating, suckling, or afflicted with disease,
should not be killed, O king, nor a doe accompanied by her child.

14.29.s:
tadadya maraṇaṃ jātaṃ mama sarvaṃ nṛpādhama ..
tava bāṇaṃ samāsādya putrasya ca mayā vinā .. 9 ..
14.29.d:
तदद्य मरणं जातं मम सर्वं नृपाधम ..
तव बाणं समासाद्य पुत्रस्य च मया विना .. 9 ..
14.29.m:
Therefore, today has death come upon me completely, O lowest of kings,
having met with your arrow, and upon my son without me.

14.29.s:
yasmādahamadharmeṇa hatā bhūmipate tvayā ..
tasmādatraiva sānau tvaṃ raudravyāghro bhaviṣyasi.. 7.3.29.10 ..
14.29.d:
यस्मादहमधर्मेण हता भूमिपते त्वया ..
तस्मादत्रैव सानौ त्वं रौद्रव्याघ्रो भविष्यसि.. 7.3.29.10 ..
14.29.m:
Since I have been killed unrighteously by you, O lord of the earth,
therefore, right here on this mountain slope, you shall become a fierce tiger!"

14.29.s:
.. pulastya uvāca .. ..
tacchrutvā sumahatpāpaṃ sa nṛpo bhayasaṃkulam ..
tāṃ vai prasādayāmāsa prāṇaśeṣāṃ tadā mṛgīm .. 11 ..
14.29.d:
.. पुलस्त्य उवाच .. ..
तच्छ्रुत्वा सुमहत्पापं स नृपो भयसंकुलम् ..
तां वै प्रसादयामास प्राणशेषां तदा मृगीम् .. 11 ..
14.29.m:
Pulastya said:
Hearing of that very great sin, that king, filled with fear,
propitiated that doe whose breath was now fading:

14.29.s:
avivekānmayā bhadre hatā tvaṃ nirghṛṇena ca ..
kuru śāpavimokṣaṃ tvaṃ tasmāddīnasya sanmṛgi .. 12 ..
14.29.d:
अविवेकान्मया भद्रे हता त्वं निर्घृणेन च ..
कुरु शापविमोक्षं त्वं तस्माद्दीनस्य सन्मृगि .. 12 ..
14.29.m:
"Out of lack of discernment and pitilessly was you killed by me, O gentle one.
Therefore, grant release from the curse to this wretched person, O good doe!"

14.29.s:
.. mṛgyuvāca .. ..
yadā tu kapilāṃ nāma drakṣyase tvaṃ payasvinīm ..
dhenuṃ tayā samālāpātprakṛtiṃ yāsyase punaḥ .. 13 ..
14.29.d:
.. मृग्युवाच .. ..
यदा तु कपिलां नाम द्रक्ष्यसे त्वं पयस्विनीम् ..
धेनुं तया समालापात्प्रकृतिं यास्यसे पुनः .. 13 ..
14.29.m:
The doe said:
"When you see a milch cow named Kapilā,
then, through conversation with her, you will return to your original nature."

14.29.s:
evamuktvā mṛgī rājāgrataḥ prāṇairvyayujyata ..
pīḍitā śaraghātena putrasnehādviśeṣataḥ .. 14 ..
14.29.d:
एवमुक्त्वा मृगी राजाग्रतः प्राणैर्व्ययुज्यत ..
पीडिता शरघातेन पुत्रस्नेहाद्विशेषतः .. 14 ..
14.29.m:
Having spoken thus before the king, the doe departed from life,
pained by the strike of the arrow and especially by love for her son.

14.29.s:
athā'sau pārthivaḥ sadyo raudrāsyaḥ samajāyata ..
vyāghro daśakarālaśca tīkṣṇadantanakhastathā ..
bhakṣayāmāsa tāṃ senāmātmīyāṃ krodhamūrcchitaḥ .. 15 ..
14.29.d:
अथाऽसौ पार्थिवः सद्यो रौद्रास्यः समजायत ..
व्याघ्रो दशकरालश्च तीक्ष्णदन्तनखस्तथा ..
भक्षयामास तां सेनामात्मीयां क्रोधमूर्च्छितः .. 15 ..

14.29.s:
tataste sainikā rājanhataśeṣāḥ suduḥkhitāḥ ..
svagṛhāṇi yayustatra yathā vṛttaṃ jane pure .. 16 ..
14.29.d:
ततस्ते सैनिका राजन्हतशेषाः सुदुःखिताः ..
स्वगृहाणि ययुस्तत्र यथा वृत्तं जने पुरे .. 16 ..
14.29.m:
Then those soldiers, O king, the survivors of the slaughter, overcome with grief,
went to their homes there, and to the people in the city [told] what had happened,

14.29.s:
nivedayanto vṛttāṃtaṃ catvareṣu trikeṣu ca ..
yathā vai vyāghratāṃ prāptaḥ sa rājā'rbudaparvate .. 17 ..
14.29.d:
निवेदयन्तो वृत्तांतं चत्वरेषु त्रिकेषु च ..
यथा वै व्याघ्रतां प्राप्तः स राजाऽर्बुदपर्वते .. 17 ..
14.29.m:
reporting the event in city squares and at crossroads,
how indeed that king had attained the state of a tiger on Mount Arbuda.

14.29.s:
tacchrutvā vacanaṃ tasya putraṃ bhūriparākramam ..
rājye'bhiṣecayāmāsu nāmnā khyātaṃ mahaujasam .. 18 ..
14.29.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं तस्य पुत्रं भूरिपराक्रमम् ..
राज्येऽभिषेचयामासु नाम्ना ख्यातं महौजसम् .. 18 ..
14.29.m:
Hearing that report, they consecrated his son of vast valor to the kingship,
renowned by name, possessing great majesty.

14.29.s:
kasyacittvatha kālasya tasminsānau nṛpottama ..
tṛṣārtaṃ gokulaṃ prāptaṃ gopagopīsamākulam .. 19 ..
14.29.d:
कस्यचित्त्वथ कालस्य तस्मिन्सानौ नृपोत्तम ..
तृषार्तं गोकुलं प्राप्तं गोपगोपीसमाकुलम् .. 19 ..
14.29.m:
Then, after some time, O best of kings, on that mountain slope
a herd of cows arrived, afflicted with thirst and crowded with cowherds and milkmaids.

14.29.s:
tatraikā gauḥ paribhraṣṭā svayūthāttṛṇatṛṣṇayā ..
kapileti ca vikhyātā svayūthasyāgragāminī.. .. 7.3.29.20 ..
14.29.d:
तत्रैका गौः परिभ्रष्टा स्वयूथात्तृणतृष्णया ..
कपिलेति च विख्याता स्वयूथस्याग्रगामिनी.. .. 7.3.29.20 ..
14.29.m:
There, one cow strayed from her herd out of longing for grass;
known as Kapilā, she was the leader of her herd.

14.29.s:
acchinnāgratṛṇaṃ yā tu sadā bhakṣayate nṛpa ..
atha sā gahvaraṃ prāptā gireḥ śūnyaṃ bhayaṃkaram .. 21 ..
14.29.d:
अच्छिन्नाग्रतृणं या तु सदा भक्षयते नृप ..
अथ सा गह्वरं प्राप्ता गिरेः शून्यं भयंकरम् .. 21 ..
14.29.m:
She who always ate uncut tips of grass, O king,
then arrived at an empty, terrifying cave on the mountain.

14.29.s:
tatrāsasāda tāṃ vyāghro daṃṣṭrotkaṭamukhāvahaḥ ..
sā taṃ dṛṣṭavatī pāpaṃ trāsamāpa mṛgīva hi .. 22 ..
14.29.d:
तत्राससाद तां व्याघ्रो दंष्ट्रोत्कटमुखावहः ..
सा तं दृष्टवती पापं त्रासमाप मृगीव हि .. 22 ..
14.29.m:
There, a tiger whose mouth was fierce with fangs approached her.
Seeing that wicked beast, she took fright like a doe,

14.29.s:
smaraṃtī gokule baddhaṃ svasutaṃ kṣīrapāyinam ..
duḥkhena rudatīṃ tāṃ sa dṛṣṭvovāca mṛgādhipaḥ .. 23 ..
14.29.d:
स्मरंती गोकुले बद्धं स्वसुतं क्षीरपायिनम् ..
दुःखेन रुदतीं तां स दृष्ट्वोवाच मृगाधिपः .. 23 ..
14.29.m:
remembering her own milk-drinking son tied in the cowpen.
Seeing her weeping in distress, that lord of beasts spoke:

14.29.s:
.. vyāghra uvāca .. ..
kiṃ vṛthā rudyate dheno māṃ prāpya na hi jīvitam ..
vidyate kasyacinmūrkhe smareṣṭāṃ devatāṃ tataḥ .. 24 .. ..
14.29.d:
.. व्याघ्र उवाच .. ..
किं वृथा रुद्यते धेनो मां प्राप्य न हि जीवितम् ..
विद्यते कस्यचिन्मूर्खे स्मरेष्टां देवतां ततः .. 24 .. ..
14.29.m:
The tiger said:
"Why weep in vain, O cow? Having encountered me, there is indeed no life
for anyone, O foolish one! Therefore, remember your chosen deity!"

14.29.s:
.. kapilovāca .. ..
svajīvitabhayādvyāghra na rodimi kathaṃcana ..
putro me bālako goṣṭhyāṃ kṣīrapāyī pratīkṣate .. 25 ..
14.29.d:
.. कपिलोवाच .. ..
स्वजीवितभयाद्व्याघ्र न रोदिमि कथंचन ..
पुत्रो मे बालको गोष्ठ्यां क्षीरपायी प्रतीक्षते .. 25 ..

14.29.s:
nādyāpi sa tṛṇā nyatti tenāhaṃ śokaviklavā ..
rodmi vyāghra sutasnehātsatyenātmānamālabhe .. 26 ..
14.29.d:
नाद्यापि स तृणा न्यत्ति तेनाहं शोकविक्लवा ..
रोद्मि व्याघ्र सुतस्नेहात्सत्येनात्मानमालभे .. 26 ..
14.29.m:
Even today he does not eat blades of grass; therefore I am overcome with grief.
I weep out of love for my son, O tiger; I touch myself with truth!

14.29.s:
pāyayitvā sutaṃ bālaṃ dṛṣṭvā pṛṣṭvā janaṃ svakam ..
punaḥ pratyāgamiṣyāmi yadi tvaṃ manyase vibho .. 27 ..
14.29.d:
पाययित्वा सुतं बालं दृष्ट्वा पृष्ट्वा जनं स्वकम् ..
पुनः प्रत्यागमिष्यामि यदि त्वं मन्यसे विभो .. 27 ..
14.29.m:
Having suckled my young son, and having seen and consulted my own kin,
I shall return again, if you agree, O mighty one."

14.29.s:
.. vyāghra uvāca .. ..
gatvā svasutasāṃnidhyaṃ dṛṣṭvātmīyaṃ ca gokulam ..
punarāgamanaṃ yatte na ca tacchraddadhāmyaham .. 28 ..
14.29.d:
.. व्याघ्र उवाच .. ..
गत्वा स्वसुतसांनिध्यं दृष्ट्वात्मीयं च गोकुलम् ..
पुनरागमनं यत्ते न च तच्छ्रद्दधाम्यहम् .. 28 ..
14.29.m:
The tiger said:
"Having gone into the presence of your own son, and having seen your own herd of cows,
that you will come back again—I do not believe that.

14.29.s:
bhayānmāṃ bhāṣase caivaṃ nāsti prāṇasamaṃ bhayam ..
tasmātprāṇabhayānna tvamāgamiṣyasi dhenuke .. 29 ..
14.29.d:
भयान्मां भाषसे चैवं नास्ति प्राणसमं भयम् ..
तस्मात्प्राणभयान्न त्वमागमिष्यसि धेनुके .. 29 ..
14.29.m:
And you speak to me thus out of fear; there is no fear equal to that for one's life.
Therefore, out of fear for your life, you will not come, O cow!"

14.29.s:
.. kapilo vāca .. ..
śapathairāgamiṣyāmi satyametacchṛṇuṣva me ..
pratyayo yadi te bhūyānmāṃ muñca tvaṃ mṛgādhipa .. 7.3.29.30 ..
14.29.d:
.. कपिलो वाच .. ..
शपथैरागमिष्यामि सत्यमेतच्छृणुष्व मे ..
प्रत्ययो यदि ते भूयान्मां मुञ्च त्वं मृगाधिप .. 7.3.29.30 ..
14.29.m: Kapilā said: / 'I will return under oaths; hear this truth from me. / If you can trust me, king of beasts, release me.'

14.29.s:
.. vyāghra uvāca .. ..
brūhi tāñchapathānbhadre samāgacchasi yaiḥ punaḥ..
tato'haṃ pratyayaṃ gatvā mocayiṣyāmi vā na vā .. 31 ..
14.29.d:
.. व्याघ्र उवाच .. ..
ब्रूहि ताञ्छपथान्भद्रे समागच्छसि यैः पुनः..
ततोऽहं प्रत्ययं गत्वा मोचयिष्यामि वा न वा .. 31 ..
14.29.m: The tiger said: / 'Speak those oaths, gentle one, by which you will return again; / then, having gained trust, I may release you or may not.'

14.29.s:
.. kapilovāca .. ..
vedādhyayanasaṃpannaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ vaṃcayettu yaḥ ..
tena pāpena lipyāmi yadyahaṃ nāgame punaḥ .. 32 ..
14.29.d:
.. कपिलोवाच .. ..
वेदाध्ययनसंपन्नं ब्राह्मणं वंचयेत्तु यः ..
तेन पापेन लिप्यामि यद्यहं नागमे पुनः .. 32 ..
14.29.m: Kapilā said: / 'He who deceives a brahmin endowed with the study of the Vedas— / may I be stained with that sin if I do not come back again.

14.29.s:
gurudroharatānāṃ ca yatpāpaṃ jāyate nṛṇām ..
tena pāpena lipyāmi yadyahaṃ nāgame punaḥ .. 33 ..
14.29.d:
गुरुद्रोहरतानां च यत्पापं जायते नृणाम् ..
तेन पापेन लिप्यामि यद्यहं नागमे पुनः .. 33 ..
14.29.m: Whatever sin is incurred by men devoted to hostility against their guru— / may I be stained with that sin if I do not come back again.

14.29.s:
yatpāpaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ hatvā gāṃ ca hatvā prajāyate ..
tena pāpena lipyāmi yadyahaṃ nāgame punaḥ .. 34 ..
14.29.d:
यत्पापं ब्राह्मणं हत्वा गां च हत्वा प्रजायते ..
तेन पापेन लिप्यामि यद्यहं नागमे पुनः .. 34 ..
14.29.m: Whatever sin arises from killing a brahmin and from killing a cow— / may I be stained with that sin if I do not come back again.

14.29.s:
mitradrohe ca yatpāpaṃ yatpāpaṃ guruvaṃcake ..
tena pāpena lipyāmi yadyahaṃ nāgame punaḥ .. 35 ..
14.29.d:
मित्रद्रोहे च यत्पापं यत्पापं गुरुवंचके ..
तेन पापेन लिप्यामि यद्यहं नागमे पुनः .. 35 ..
14.29.m: Whatever sin is incurred in betraying a friend, whatever sin in deceiving a guru— / may I be stained with that sin if I do not come back again.

14.29.s:
yo gāṃ spṛśati pādena brāhmaṇaṃ pāvakaṃ tathā ..
tena pāpena lipyāmi yadyahaṃ nāgame punaḥ .. 36 ..
14.29.d:
यो गां स्पृशति पादेन ब्राह्मणं पावकं तथा ..
तेन पापेन लिप्यामि यद्यहं नागमे पुनः .. 36 ..
14.29.m: Whoever touches a cow with the foot, or a brahmin, or fire— / may I be stained with that sin if I do not come back again.

14.29.s:
kūpārāmataḍāgānāṃ yo bhaṃgaṃ kuruta naraḥ ..
tena pāpena lipyāmi yadyahaṃ nāgame punaḥ .. 37 ..
14.29.d:
कूपारामतडागानां यो भंगं कुरुत नरः ..
तेन पापेन लिप्यामि यद्यहं नागमे पुनः .. 37 ..
14.29.m: The man who destroys wells, pleasure gardens, or ponds— / may I be stained with that sin if I do not come back again.

14.29.s:
kṛtaghnasya ca yatpāpaṃ sūcakasya ca yadbhavet ..
tena pāpena lipyāmi yadyahaṃ nāgame punaḥ .. 38 ..
14.29.d:
कृतघ्नस्य च यत्पापं सूचकस्य च यद्भवेत् ..
तेन पापेन लिप्यामि यद्यहं नागमे पुनः .. 38 ..
14.29.m: Whatever sin belongs to the ungrateful, and whatever belongs to an informer— / may I be stained with that sin if I do not come back again.

14.29.s:
madyamāṃsaratānāṃ ca yatpāpaṃ jāyate nṛṇām ..
tena pāpena lipyāmi yadyahaṃ nāgame punaḥ .. 39 ..
14.29.d:
मद्यमांसरतानां च यत्पापं जायते नृणाम् ..
तेन पापेन लिप्यामि यद्यहं नागमे पुनः .. 39 ..
14.29.m: Whatever sin is incurred by men devoted to liquor and meat— / may I be stained with that sin if I do not come back again.

14.29.s:
rājapaiśunyakartṝṇāṃ yatpāpaṃ jāyate nṛṇām ..
tena pāpena lipyāmi yadyahaṃ nāgame punaḥ .. 7.3.29.40 ..
14.29.d:
राजपैशुन्यकर्तॄणां यत्पापं जायते नृणाम् ..
तेन पापेन लिप्यामि यद्यहं नागमे पुनः .. 7.3.29.40 ..
14.29.m: Whatever sin is incurred by men who commit slander before the king— / may I be stained with that sin if I do not come back again.

14.29.s:
vedavikrayakartṝṇāṃ yatpāpaṃ saṃprajāyate ..
tena pāpena lipyāmi yadyahaṃ nāgame punaḥ .. 41 ..
14.29.d:
वेदविक्रयकर्तॄणां यत्पापं संप्रजायते ..
तेन पापेन लिप्यामि यद्यहं नागमे पुनः .. 41 ..
14.29.m: Whatever sin is incurred by those who sell the Vedas— / may I be stained with that sin if I do not come back again.

14.29.s:
dīyamānaṃ dvijātīnāṃ nivārayati yo'lpadhīḥ ..
tena pāpena lipyāmi yadyahaṃ nāgame punaḥ .. 42 ..
14.29.d:
दीयमानं द्विजातीनां निवारयति योऽल्पधीः ..
तेन पापेन लिप्यामि यद्यहं नागमे पुनः .. 42 ..
14.29.m: That small-minded man who obstructs what is being given to the twice-born— / may I be stained with that sin if I do not come back again.

14.29.s:
viśvastaghātakānāṃ ca yatpāpaṃ samudāhṛtam ..
tena pāpena lipyāmi yadyahaṃ nāgame punaḥ .. 43 ..
14.29.d:
विश्वस्तघातकानां च यत्पापं समुदाहृतम् ..
तेन पापेन लिप्यामि यद्यहं नागमे पुनः .. 43 ..
14.29.m: Whatever sin is declared of murderers of the trusting— / may I be stained with that sin if I do not come back again.

14.29.s:
dvijadveṣaratānāṃ hi yatpāpaṃ jāyate nṛṇām ..
tena pāpena lipyāmi yadyahaṃ nāgame punaḥ .. 44 ..
14.29.d:
द्विजद्वेषरतानां हि यत्पापं जायते नृणाम् ..
तेन पापेन लिप्यामि यद्यहं नागमे पुनः .. 44 ..
14.29.m: Whatever sin is incurred by men devoted to hatred of the twice-born— / may I be stained with that sin if I do not come back again.

14.29.s:
paravādaratānāṃ ca pāpaṃ yacca durātmanām ..
tena pāpena lipyāmi yadyahaṃ nāgame punaḥ .. .. 45 ..
14.29.d:
परवादरतानां च पापं यच्च दुरात्मनाम् ..
तेन पापेन लिप्यामि यद्यहं नागमे पुनः .. .. 45 ..
14.29.m: Whatever sin belongs to the wicked devoted to slandering others— / may I be stained with that sin if I do not come back again.

14.29.s:
rātrau ye pāpakarmāṇo bhakṣaṃti dadhisaktukān ..
tena pāpena lipyāmi yadyahaṃ nāgame punaḥ .. 46 ..
14.29.d:
रात्रौ ये पापकर्माणो भक्षंति दधिसक्तुकान् ..
तेन पापेन लिप्यामि यद्यहं नागमे पुनः .. 46 ..
14.29.m: Those evil-doers who eat curd and barley groats at night— / may I be stained with that sin if I do not come back again.

14.29.s:
vṛṃtākaṃ mūlakaṃ śvetaṃ raktaṃ ye'śnaṃti gṛṃjanam ..
tena pāpena lipyāmi yadyahaṃ nāgame punaḥ .. 47 ..
14.29.d:
वृंताकं मूलकं श्वेतं रक्तं येऽश्नंति गृंजनम् ..
तेन पापेन लिप्यामि यद्यहं नागमे पुनः .. 47 ..
14.29.m: Those who eat aubergine, white radish, or red carrot— / may I be stained with that sin if I do not come back again.'

14.29.s:
.. pulastya uvāca .. ..
sa tasyāḥ śapathāñchrutvā vismayotphullalocanaḥ ..
pratyayaṃ ca tadā gatvā vyāghro vākyamathābravīt .. 48 ..
14.29.d:
.. पुलस्त्य उवाच .. ..
स तस्याः शपथाञ्छ्रुत्वा विस्मयोत्फुल्ललोचनः ..
प्रत्ययं च तदा गत्वा व्याघ्रो वाक्यमथाब्रवीत् .. 48 ..
14.29.m: Pulastya said: / Hearing her oaths, his eyes wide with amazement, / and having then gained trust, the tiger said these words:

14.29.s:
.. vyāghra uvāca .. ..
gaccha tvaṃ gokule bhadre punarāgamanaṃ kuru ..
na caitadavagaṃtavyaṃ yadayaṃ vañcito mayā .. 49 ..
14.29.d:
.. व्याघ्र उवाच .. ..
गच्छ त्वं गोकुले भद्रे पुनरागमनं कुरु ..
न चैतदवगंतव्यं यदयं वञ्चितो मया .. 49 ..
14.29.m: The tiger said: / 'Go to your cow-station, gentle one, and make your return. / And it must not be thought: "He has been deceived by me."

14.29.s:
kapile gaccha paśya tvaṃ tanayaṃ sutavatsale ..
pāyayitvā stanaṃ pūrṇamavaghrāya ca mūrdhani .. 7.3.29.50 ..
14.29.d:
कपिले गच्छ पश्य त्वं तनयं सुतवत्सले ..
पाययित्वा स्तनं पूर्णमवघ्राय च मूर्धनि .. 7.3.29.50 ..
14.29.m: Go, Kapilā, see your calf, you who are fond of your offspring; / after letting him suck your full udder and sniffing his head,

14.29.s:
mātaraṃ bhrātaraṃ dṛṣṭvā sakhīḥ svajanavabāṃdhavān ..
satyamevāgrataḥ kṛtvā nānyathā kartumarhasi .. 51 ..
14.29.d:
मातरं भ्रातरं दृष्ट्वा सखीः स्वजनवबांधवान् ..
सत्यमेवाग्रतः कृत्वा नान्यथा कर्तुमर्हसि .. 51 ..
14.29.m: having seen your mother, brother, female companions, kin, and relatives, / keep only truth foremost; you must not do otherwise.'

14.29.s:
.. pulastya uvāca .. ..
sā'nujñātā mṛgendreṇa kapilā putravatsalā ...
aśrupūrṇamukhī dīnā prasthitā gokulaṃ prati .. 52 ..
14.29.d:
.. पुलस्त्य उवाच .. ..
साऽनुज्ञाता मृगेन्द्रेण कपिला पुत्रवत्सला ...
अश्रुपूर्णमुखी दीना प्रस्थिता गोकुलं प्रति .. 52 ..
14.29.m: Pulastya said: / Permitted by the lion among beasts, Kapilā, fond of her offspring, / her face filled with tears and miserable, set out toward the cow-station.

14.29.s:
vepamānā bhayodvignā śokasāgaramadhyagā ..
kariṇīva hi raudreṇa hariṇā sā balīyasā ...
tataḥ svagokulaṃ prāptā rabhamāṇā muhurmuhuḥ .. 53 ..
14.29.d:
वेपमाना भयोद्विग्ना शोकसागरमध्यगा ..
करिणीव हि रौद्रेण हरिणा सा बलीयसा ...
ततः स्वगोकुलं प्राप्ता रभमाणा मुहुर्मुहुः .. 53 ..
14.29.m: Trembling, distressed with fear, sunk in an ocean of grief / like a female elephant seized by a terrifying and powerful lion, / she then reached her cow-station, lowing again and again.

14.29.s:
tasyāḥ śabdaṃ tataḥ śrutvā jñātvā vatsaḥ svamātaram ..
sammukhaḥ prayayau tūrṇamūrddhvapucchaḥ praharṣitaḥ .. 54 ..
14.29.d:
तस्याः शब्दं ततः श्रुत्वा ज्ञात्वा वत्सः स्वमातरम् ..
सम्मुखः प्रययौ तूर्णमूर्द्ध्वपुच्छः प्रहर्षितः .. 54 ..
14.29.m: Then, hearing her voice and recognising his mother, / the calf eagerly ran to face her with tail raised, highly delighted.

14.29.s:
akālāgamanaṃ tasyā raudraṃ bhaṃbhāravaṃ tathā ..
dṛṣṭvā śrutvā ca vatso'sau śaṃkitaḥ paripṛcchati .. 55 ..
14.29.d:
अकालागमनं तस्या रौद्रं भंभारवं तथा ..
दृष्ट्वा श्रुत्वा च वत्सोऽसौ शंकितः परिपृच्छति .. 55 ..
14.29.m: Seeing her untimely arrival and hearing her dreadful lowing, / that calf, filled with misgiving, asked:

14.29.s:
.. vatsa uvāca .. ..
na te paśyāmi saumyatvaṃ durmanā iva lakṣyame ..
kimarthamanyavelāyāṃ samāyātā vadasva me .. 56 ..
14.29.d:
.. वत्स उवाच .. ..
न ते पश्यामि सौम्यत्वं दुर्मना इव लक्ष्यमे ..
किमर्थमन्यवेलायां समायाता वदस्व मे .. 56 ..
14.29.m: The calf said: / 'I see no serenity in you; you appear as if broken-hearted. / Why have you arrived at an unusual hour? Tell me!'

14.29.s:
.. kapilovāca .. ..
piba putra stanaṃ paścātkāraṇaṃ cāpi me śṛṇu ..
āgatā'haṃ tava snehātkuru tṛptiṃ yathepsitām ..57 ..
14.29.d:
.. कपिलोवाच .. ..
पिब पुत्र स्तनं पश्चात्कारणं चापि मे शृणु ..
आगताऽहं तव स्नेहात्कुरु तृप्तिं यथेप्सिताम् ..57 ..
14.29.m: Kapilā said: / 'Drink from the udder, son; hear also the cause from me afterward. / I have come out of love for you; take your desired satisfaction.

14.29.s:
apaścimamidaṃ putra durlabhaṃ mātṛdarśanam ..
mayā'dya putra gaṃtavyaṃ śapathairāgatā yataḥ ..58..
14.29.d:
अपश्चिममिदं पुत्र दुर्लभं मातृदर्शनम् ..
मयाऽद्य पुत्र गंतव्यं शपथैरागता यतः ..58..
14.29.m: This is the very last and rare sight of your mother, son. / Today I must go, son, since I came under oaths.

14.29.s:
vyāghrasya kāmarūpasya dātavyaṃ jīvitaṃ mayā ..
tenāhaṃ śapathairmuktā kāraṇāttava putraka .. 59 ..
14.29.d:
व्याघ्रस्य कामरूपस्य दातव्यं जीवितं मया ..
तेनाहं शपथैर्मुक्ता कारणात्तव पुत्रक .. 59 ..
14.29.m: My life must be given to a shape-shifting tiger. / By him I was released under oaths on your account, my child.

14.29.s:
mayā'dya tatra gaṃtavyaṃ mṛgarājasamīpataḥ ..
yadā ca śapathaiḥ putra dāsyāmi ca kalevaram ..7.3.29.60..
14.29.d:
मयाऽद्य तत्र गंतव्यं मृगराजसमीपतः ..
यदा च शपथैः पुत्र दास्यामि च कलेवरम् ..7.3.29.60..
14.29.m: Today I must go there, to the proximity of the king of beasts; / and in accordance with the oaths, son, I will surrender my body.'

14.29.s:
.. vatsa uvāca .. ..
ahaṃ tatra gamiṣyāmi yatra tvaṃ gaṃtumicchasi ..
ślāghyaṃ hi maraṇaṃ me'dya tvayā saha na saṃśayaḥ ..61..
14.29.d:
.. वत्स उवाच .. ..
अहं तत्र गमिष्यामि यत्र त्वं गंतुमिच्छसि ..
श्लाघ्यं हि मरणं मेऽद्य त्वया सह न संशयः ..61..
14.29.m: The calf said: / 'I will go there where you wish to go; / for death today together with you is indeed praiseworthy, without doubt.

14.29.s:
ekākinā'pi marttavyaṃ yasmānmayā tvayā vinā ..
yadi māṃ sahitaṃ tatra tvayā vyāghro vadhiṣyati ..62..
14.29.d:
एकाकिनाऽपि मर्त्तव्यं यस्मान्मया त्वया विना ..
यदि मां सहितं तत्र त्वया व्याघ्रो वधिष्यति ..62..
14.29.m: For I must die even alone without you; / if the tiger kills me there along with you,

14.29.s:
yā gatirmātṛbhaktānāṃ dhruvaṃ sā me bhaviṣyati ..
tasmādavaśyaṃ yāsyāmi tvayā saha na saṃśayaḥ .. 63 ..
14.29.d:
या गतिर्मातृभक्तानां ध्रुवं सा मे भविष्यति ..
तस्मादवश्यं यास्यामि त्वया सह न संशयः .. 63 ..
14.29.m: whatever realm belongs to those devoted to their mother, that will surely be mine. / Therefore I will certainly go with you, without a doubt.

14.29.s:
athavā'traiva tiṣṭha tvaṃ śapathāḥ saṃtu me tava ..
tava sthāne prayāsyāmi mātastvaṃ yadi manyase .. 64 ..
14.29.d:
अथवाऽत्रैव तिष्ठ त्वं शपथाः संतु मे तव ..
तव स्थाने प्रयास्यामि मातस्त्वं यदि मन्यसे .. 64 ..
14.29.m: Or else remain right here; let your oaths fall upon me. / I will go in your place, mother, if you approve.

14.29.s:
jananyā viprayuktasya jīvitaṃ na hi me priyam ..
nāsti mātṛsamaḥ kaścidbālānāṃ kṣīrajīvinām .. 65 ..
14.29.d:
जनन्या विप्रयुक्तस्य जीवितं न हि मे प्रियम् ..
नास्ति मातृसमः कश्चिद्बालानां क्षीरजीविनाम् .. 65 ..
14.29.m: Separated from my mother, life is indeed not dear to me; / for young ones living on milk, no one is equal to a mother.

14.29.s:
nāsti mātṛsamo nātho nāsti mātṛsamā gatiḥ ..
ye mātṛniratāḥ putrāste yāṃti paramāṃ gatim .. 66 ..
14.29.d:
नास्ति मातृसमो नाथो नास्ति मातृसमा गतिः ..
ये मातृनिरताः पुत्रास्ते यांति परमां गतिम् .. 66 ..
14.29.m: There is no protector equal to a mother; there is no refuge equal to a mother. / Those sons who are devoted to their mother go to the supreme goal.'

14.29.s:
.. kapilovāca .. ..
mamaiva vihito mṛtyurna te putraka sāṃpratam ..
na cāyamanyabhūtānāṃ mṛtyuḥ syādanyamṛtyutaḥ .. 67 ..
14.29.d:
.. कपिलोवाच .. ..
ममैव विहितो मृत्युर्न ते पुत्रक सांप्रतम् ..
न चायमन्यभूतानां मृत्युः स्यादन्यमृत्युतः .. 67 ..
14.29.m: Kapilā said: / 'Death is ordained for me alone, child, not for you now; / nor can the death of other creatures occur through the death of another.

14.29.s:
apaścimamidaṃ putra mātuḥ sandeśamuttamam ..
śṛṇuṣvāvahito bhūtvā pariṇāmasukhāvaham .. 68 ..
14.29.d:
अपश्चिममिदं पुत्र मातुः सन्देशमुत्तमम् ..
शृणुष्वावहितो भूत्वा परिणामसुखावहम् .. 68 ..
14.29.m: Listen attentively, son, to this last excellent advice of your mother, / which brings happiness in the end:

14.29.s:
vane cara sadā vatsa apramādaparo bhava ..
pramādātsarvabhūtāni vinaśyaṃti na saṃśayaḥ .. 69 ..
14.29.d:
वने चर सदा वत्स अप्रमादपरो भव ..
प्रमादात्सर्वभूतानि विनश्यंति न संशयः .. 69 ..
14.29.m: Wander always in the forest, calf, intent on vigilance; / through heedlessness all living creatures perish, without doubt.

14.29.s:
na ca lobhena cartavyaṃ viṣamasthaṃ tṛṇaṃ kvacit ..
lobhādvināśo jaṃtūnāmiha loke paratra ca .. 7.3.29.70 ..
14.29.d:
न च लोभेन चर्तव्यं विषमस्थं तृणं क्वचित् ..
लोभाद्विनाशो जंतूनामिह लोके परत्र च .. 7.3.29.70 ..
14.29.m: Nor should you graze on grass in a perilous spot anywhere out of greed; / from greed comes the destruction of creatures in this world and the next.

14.29.s:
samudramaṭavīṃ yuddhaṃ viśaṃte lobhamohitāḥ ..
lobhādi kāryamatyugraṃ kurvaṃti tyājya eva saḥ .. 71 ..
14.29.d:
समुद्रमटवीं युद्धं विशंते लोभमोहिताः ..
लोभादि कार्यमत्युग्रं कुर्वंति त्याज्य एव सः .. 71 ..
14.29.m: Deluded by greed, they enter the ocean, the dense forest, and war; / out of greed and the like they commit terrifying deeds; it must certainly be abandoned.'

14.29.s:
lobhātpramādādāśvāsātpuruṣo bādhyate tribhiḥ ..
tasmāllobho na karttavyo na pramādo na viśvaset .. 72 ..
14.29.d:
लोभात्प्रमादादाश्वासात्पुरुषो बाध्यते त्रिभिः ..
तस्माल्लोभो न कर्त्तव्यो न प्रमादो न विश्वसेत् .. 72 ..
14.29.m: A man is ruined by three things: by greed, by carelessness, and by false confidence. / Therefore, one should not be greedy, nor careless, nor overly trusting.

14.29.s:
ātmā ca satataṃ putra rakṣitavyaḥ prayatnataḥ ..
sarvebhyaḥ śvāpadebhyaśca mlecchebhyastaskarāditaḥ ..73..
14.29.d:
आत्मा च सततं पुत्र रक्षितव्यः प्रयत्नतः ..
सर्वेभ्यः श्वापदेभ्यश्च म्लेच्छेभ्यस्तस्करादितः ..73..
14.29.m: And oneself, O son, must always be protected with great effort / from all beasts of prey, from barbarians, and from thieves and the like,

14.29.s:
tiryagbhyaḥ pāpayonibhyaḥ sadā vicaratā vane ..
na ca śokastvayā kāryaḥ sarveṣāṃ maraṇaṃ dhuvam .. 74 ..
14.29.d:
तिर्यग्भ्यः पापयोनिभ्यः सदा विचरता वने ..
न च शोकस्त्वया कार्यः सर्वेषां मरणं धुवम् .. 74 ..
14.29.m: as well as from animals born of sinful wombs, as you constantly roam in the forest. / Nor should you grieve; death is certain for everyone.

14.29.s:
asmākaṃ prativācaṃ ca śṛṇu śokavināśinīm ..
yathā hi pathikaḥ kaścicchāyārthī vṛkṣamāsthitaḥ ..
viśrāntaśca punaryāti tadvadbhūtasamāgamaḥ .. 75 ..
14.29.d:
अस्माकं प्रतिवाचं च शृणु शोकविनाशिनीम् ..
यथा हि पथिकः कश्चिच्छायार्थी वृक्षमास्थितः ..
विश्रान्तश्च पुनर्याति तद्वद्भूतसमागमः .. 75 ..
14.29.m: Hear also my reply, which dispels grief: / Just as a traveler seeking shade rests under a tree, / and having rested, moves on again, so is the meeting of living beings.

14.29.s:
.. pulastya uvāca .. ..
evaṃ saṃbhāṣya taṃ vatsamavaghrāya ca mūrddhani ..
svamātaraṃ sakhīvargaṃ tato draṣṭuṃ samāgatā .. 76 ..
14.29.d:
.. पुलस्त्य उवाच .. ..
एवं संभाष्य तं वत्समवघ्राय च मूर्द्धनि ..
स्वमातरं सखीवर्गं ततो द्रष्टुं समागता .. 76 ..
14.29.m: Pulastya said: / Having spoken thus to that calf and sniffed [him] on the crown of his head, / she then went to see her own mother and the group of her companions.

14.29.s:
abravīcca tato vākyaṃ putraśokena duḥkhitā ..
aṃbāḥ śṛṇuta me vākyamapaścimamidaṃ sphuṭam .. 77 ..
14.29.d:
अब्रवीच्च ततो वाक्यं पुत्रशोकेन दुःखिता ..
अंबाः शृणुत मे वाक्यमपश्चिममिदं स्फुटम् .. 77 ..
14.29.m: And then, distressed with grief for her son, she spoke these words: / 'O mothers, clearly hear these final words of mine:

14.29.s:
anāthamabalaṃ dīnaṃ phenapaṃ mama putrakam ..
mātṛśokābhisaṃtaptaṃ sarvāstaṃ pālayiṣyatha .. 78 ..
14.29.d:
अनाथमबलं दीनं फेनपं मम पुत्रकम् ..
मातृशोकाभिसंतप्तं सर्वास्तं पालयिष्यथ .. 78 ..
14.29.m: My little son is helpless, weak, poor, and drinks only froth. / Tormented by grief for his mother, you all must protect him.

14.29.s:
bhāvinīnāmayaṃ putraḥ sāṃprataṃ ca viśeṣataḥ ..
snapanīyaḥ pāyitavyaḥ poṣyaḥ pālyaḥ svaputravat .. 79 ..
14.29.d:
भाविनीनामयं पुत्रः सांप्रतं च विशेषतः ..
स्नपनीयः पायितव्यः पोष्यः पाल्यः स्वपुत्रवत् .. 79 ..
14.29.m: He is the son of you fortunate ones, especially now. / He must be bathed, given drink, nourished, and protected like your own son.

14.29.s:
caraṃtaṃ viṣame sthāne caraṃtaṃ paragokule ..
akāryeṣu pravartaṃtaṃ he sakhyo vārayiṣyatha .. 7.3.29.80 ..
14.29.d:
चरंतं विषमे स्थाने चरंतं परगोकुले ..
अकार्येषु प्रवर्तंतं हे सख्यो वारयिष्यथ .. 7.3.29.80 ..
14.29.m: If he wanders in rough places, or into another's herd, / or engages in improper actions, O friends, you must restrain him.

14.29.s:
kṣamadhvaṃ ca mahābhāgā yāsye'haṃ satyasaṃśrayāt ..
yatrā'sau tiṣṭhate vyāghro muktā'haṃ yena sāṃpratam .. 81..
14.29.d:
क्षमध्वं च महाभागा यास्येऽहं सत्यसंश्रयात् ..
यत्राऽसौ तिष्ठते व्याघ्रो मुक्ताऽहं येन सांप्रतम् .. 81..
14.29.m: And forgive me, O fortunate ones; relying on truth, I shall go / where that tiger waits, by whom I was just released.'

14.29.s:
sarvāstā vacanaṃ śrutvā tasyāḥ śokasamanvitāḥ ..
viṣādaṃ paramaṃ gatvā vākyamūcuḥ suduḥkhitāḥ.. 82..
14.29.d:
सर्वास्ता वचनं श्रुत्वा तस्याः शोकसमन्विताः ..
विषादं परमं गत्वा वाक्यमूचुः सुदुःखिताः.. 82..
14.29.m: Having heard her words, filled with grief, / they all fell into deep dejection and spoke, greatly sorrowful:

14.29.s:
kapile naiva gaṃtavyaṃ na te doṣo bhaviṣyati..
prāṇātyaye na doṣo'sti saṃparāye ca dāruṇe.. 83..
14.29.d:
कपिले नैव गंतव्यं न ते दोषो भविष्यति..
प्राणात्यये न दोषोऽस्ति संपराये च दारुणे.. 83..
14.29.m: 'O Kapilā, you must not go at all; no fault will attach to you. / There is no fault when life is in peril and in dread calamity.

14.29.s:
atra gāthā purā gītā munibhirdharmavādibhiḥ..
prāṇātyaye samutpanne śapathe nāsti pātakam.. 84..
14.29.d:
अत्र गाथा पुरा गीता मुनिभिर्धर्मवादिभिः..
प्राणात्यये समुत्पन्ने शपथे नास्ति पातकम्.. 84..
14.29.m: In this regard, a verse was sung of old by sages who expound righteousness: / "When life is in danger, there is no sin in an oath [broken]."'

14.29.s:
kapilovāca..
prāṇināṃ prāṇa rakṣārthaṃ vadāmyevānṛtaṃ vacaḥ ..
nātmārthamupayuñjāmi svalpamapyanṛtaṃ kvacit .. 85 ..
14.29.d:
कपिलोवाच..
प्राणिनां प्राण रक्षार्थं वदाम्येवानृतं वचः ..
नात्मार्थमुपयुञ्जामि स्वल्पमप्यनृतं क्वचित् .. 85 ..
14.29.m: Kapilā said: / 'Only to protect the lives of living beings do I speak an untrue word. / For my own sake, I never utter even the slightest lie.

14.29.s:
aśvamedhasahasraṃ tu satyaṃ ca tulayā dhṛtam ..
aśvamedhasahasrāddhi satyameva viśiṣyate .. 86 ..
14.29.d:
अश्वमेधसहस्रं तु सत्यं च तुलया धृतम् ..
अश्वमेधसहस्राद्धि सत्यमेव विशिष्यते .. 86 ..
14.29.m: A thousand horse-sacrifices and truth were weighed on a balance: / truth indeed outweighs a thousand horse-sacrifices.

14.29.s:
tasmānnānṛtamātmānaṃ kariṣye jīvitāśayā ..
ājñāpayatu māmāryā yāsye yatra mṛgādhipaḥ .. 87 ..
14.29.d:
तस्मान्नानृतमात्मानं करिष्ये जीविताशया ..
आज्ञापयतु मामार्या यास्ये यत्र मृगाधिपः .. 87 ..
14.29.m: Therefore, through desire for life, I will not make myself untrue. / Let the noble lady permit me; I shall go where the king of beasts is.'

14.29.s:
.. vayasyā ūcuḥ .. ..
kapile tvaṃ namaskāryā sarvairapi surāsuraiḥ ..
yattvaṃ paramasatyena prāṇāṃstyajasi dustyajān .. 88 ..
14.29.d:
.. वयस्या ऊचुः .. ..
कपिले त्वं नमस्कार्या सर्वैरपि सुरासुरैः ..
यत्त्वं परमसत्येन प्राणांस्त्यजसि दुस्त्यजान् .. 88 ..
14.29.m: Her companions said: / 'O Kapilā, you are worthy of reverence even by all gods and asuras, / since through supreme truth you abandon your life, which is so hard to give up.

14.29.s:
avaśyaṃ na ca te bhāvī mṛtyuḥ satyātkathaṃcana ..
pramāṇaṃ yadi satyaṃ hi vraja paṃthāḥ śivo'stu te .. 89 ..
14.29.d:
अवश्यं न च ते भावी मृत्युः सत्यात्कथंचन ..
प्रमाणं यदि सत्यं हि व्रज पंथाः शिवोऽस्तु ते .. 89 ..
14.29.m: Surely, by virtue of truth, death shall not befall you in any way. / If truth is indeed the authority, go! May your path be auspicious!'

14.29.s:
.. pulastya uvāca .. ..
evamuktā ca kapilā gatā yatra mṛgādhipaḥ ..
athāsau kapilāṃ dṛṣṭvā vismayotphullalocanaḥ ..
abravītpraśritaṃ vākyaṃ harṣagadgadayā girā .. 7.3.29.90 ..
14.29.d:
.. पुलस्त्य उवाच .. ..
एवमुक्ता च कपिला गता यत्र मृगाधिपः ..
अथासौ कपिलां दृष्ट्वा विस्मयोत्फुल्ललोचनः ..
अब्रवीत्प्रश्रितं वाक्यं हर्षगद्गदया गिरा .. 7.3.29.90 ..
14.29.m: Pulastya said: / Spoken to in this manner, Kapilā went to where the king of beasts was. / Then, seeing Kapilā, his eyes widened with astonishment, / and he spoke modest words in a voice faltering with joy.

14.29.s:
.. vyāghra uvāca .. ..
svāgataṃ tava kalyāṇi kapile satyavādini ..
nahi satyavatāṃ kiṃcidaśubhaṃ vidyate kvacit .. 91 ..
14.29.d:
.. व्याघ्र उवाच .. ..
स्वागतं तव कल्याणि कपिले सत्यवादिनि ..
नहि सत्यवतां किंचिदशुभं विद्यते क्वचित् .. 91 ..
14.29.m: The tiger said: / 'Welcome to you, O auspicious one, O truthful Kapilā! / For nothing inauspicious ever exists anywhere for the truthful.

14.29.s:
tvayoktaṃ kapile pūrvaṃ śapathairāgamāya ca ..
tena me kautukaṃ jātaṃ yātā''gacchetpunaḥ katham .. 92 ..
14.29.d:
त्वयोक्तं कपिले पूर्वं शपथैरागमाय च ..
तेन मे कौतुकं जातं याता'ऽगच्छेत्पुनः कथम् .. 92 ..
14.29.m: You spoke previously with oaths, O Kapilā, in order to return; / because of that, curiosity arose in me: "How could one who has gone return again?"

14.29.s:
tasmādgaccha mayā muktā yatrā'sau tanayastava ..
tiṣṭhate gokule baddhaḥ kṣīrapāyī suduḥkhitaḥ ..93.. ..
14.29.d:
तस्माद्गच्छ मया मुक्ता यत्राऽसौ तनयस्तव ..
तिष्ठते गोकुले बद्धः क्षीरपायी सुदुःखितः ..93.. ..
14.29.m: Therefore, released by me, go to where that son of yours / stays, tied up in the herd of cattle, drinking milk and deeply distressed.'

14.29.s:
.. pulastya uvāca .. ..
etasminneva kāle tu sa rājā prakṛtiṃ gataḥ ..
mṛgīśāpena nirmukto divyarūpavapurdharaḥ ..
tato'bravītprahṛṣṭātmā kapilāṃ satyavādinīm .. 94 ..
14.29.d:
.. पुलस्त्य उवाच .. ..
एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु स राजा प्रकृतिं गतः ..
मृगीशापेन निर्मुक्तो दिव्यरूपवपुर्धरः ..
ततोऽब्रवीत्प्रहृष्टात्मा कपिलां सत्यवादिनीम् .. 94 ..
14.29.m: Pulastya said: / At that very moment, that king returned to his natural form, / freed from the doe's curse and possessing a divine form and body. / Then, delighted in heart, he spoke to the truthful Kapilā.

14.29.s:
.. rājovāca .. ..
prasādāttava mukto'haṃ śāpādasmātsudāruṇāt ..
kiṃ te priyaṃ karomyadya dhenuke brūhi satvaram .. 95 ..
14.29.d:
.. राजोवाच .. ..
प्रसादात्तव मुक्तोऽहं शापादस्मात्सुदारुणात् ..
किं ते प्रियं करोम्यद्य धेनुके ब्रूहि सत्वरम् .. 95 ..
14.29.m: The king said: / 'By your grace, I am freed from this terrible curse. / What agreeable thing shall I do for you today, O little cow? Speak quickly!'

14.29.s:
.. kapilovāca .. ..
kṛtakṛtyā'smi rājenda yattvaṃ mukto'si kilbiṣāt..
pipāsā bādhatetyarthaṃ sāṃprataṃ jalamānayam .. 96 ..
14.29.d:
.. कपिलोवाच .. ..
कृतकृत्याऽस्मि राजेन्द यत्त्वं मुक्तोऽसि किल्बिषात्..
पिपासा बाधतेत्यर्थं सांप्रतं जलमानयम् .. 96 ..
14.29.m: Kapilā said: / 'I have achieved my purpose, O king of kings, since you are freed from sin. / Thirst torments me exceedingly; bring water now.

14.29.s: naivānṛtaṃ vijānīhi satyametanmayoditam .. 97 ..
14.29.d: नैवानृतं विजानीहि सत्यमेतन्मयोदितम् .. 97 ..
14.29.m: Do not think this untrue; this spoken by me is the truth.'

14.29.s:
.. pulastya uvāca .. ..
athāsau pārthivo haste cāpamādāya satvaram ..
sajyaṃ kṛtvā śaraṃ gṛhya jaghāna dharaṇītalam .. 98 ..
14.29.d:
.. पुलस्त्य उवाच .. ..
अथासौ पार्थिवो हस्ते चापमादाय सत्वरम् ..
सज्यं कृत्वा शरं गृह्य जघान धरणीतलम् .. 98 ..
14.29.m: Pulastya said: / Then that king, quickly taking his bow in hand, / strung it, took an arrow, and struck the surface of the earth.

14.29.s:
tataḥ salilamuttasthau nirmalaṃ śītalaṃ śubham ..
tatra sā kapilā snātvā vitṛṣā samapadyata .. 99 ..
14.29.d:
ततः सलिलमुत्तस्थौ निर्मलं शीतलं शुभम् ..
तत्र सा कपिला स्नात्वा वितृषा समपद्यत .. 99 ..
14.29.m: Then pure, cool, and auspicious water welled up. / There Kapilā bathed and became free of thirst.

14.29.s:
etasminnantare dharmaḥ svayaṃ tatra samāgataḥ ..
abravītkapilāṃ hṛṣṭo varaṃ varaya śobhane ..7.3.29.100 ..
14.29.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे धर्मः स्वयं तत्र समागतः ..
अब्रवीत्कपिलां हृष्टो वरं वरय शोभने ..7.3.29.100 ..
14.29.m: In the meantime, Dharma himself arrived there / and, delighted, said to Kapilā: 'Choose a boon, O beautiful one!

14.29.s:
tava satyena tuṣṭo'haṃ nāsti te sadṛśī kvacit ..
trailokye sakale dhenurna bhaviṣyati vai śubhe .. 101 ..
14.29.d:
तव सत्येन तुष्टोऽहं नास्ति ते सदृशी क्वचित् ..
त्रैलोक्ये सकले धेनुर्न भविष्यति वै शुभे .. 101 ..
14.29.m: I am pleased with your truthfulness. In the entire three worlds, O auspicious one, / there is no cow equal to you anywhere, nor will there ever be.'

14.29.s:
.. kapilovāca .. ..
prasādāttava gaccheya saha rājñā sagokulā ..
suprabheṇa padaṃ divyaṃ jarāmaraṇavarjitam.. 102 ..
14.29.d:
.. कपिलोवाच .. ..
प्रसादात्तव गच्छेय सह राज्ञा सगोकुला ..
सुप्रभेण पदं दिव्यं जरामरणवर्जितम्.. 102 ..
14.29.m: Kapilā said: / 'By your favor, along with the king, together with the herd of cows / and with Suprabha, may I go to the divine abode free from old age and death.

14.29.s:
mannāmnā khyātimāyātu puṇyametajjalāśayam ..
sarvapāpaharaṃ nṛṇāṃ sarvakāmapradaṃ tathā .. 103 ..
14.29.d:
मन्नाम्ना ख्यातिमायातु पुण्यमेतज्जलाशयम् ..
सर्वपापहरं नृणां सर्वकामप्रदं तथा .. 103 ..
14.29.m: May this sacred reservoir attain renown by my name, / removing all sins of men and granting all desires.'

14.29.s:
.. dharma uvāca .. ..
ye'tra snānaṃ kariṣyaṃti supuṇye salile śubhe ..
caturddaśyāṃ viśeṣeṇa te yāsyaṃti parāṃ gatim .. 104 ..
14.29.d:
.. धर्म उवाच .. ..
येऽत्र स्नानं करिष्यंति सुपुण्ये सलिले शुभे ..
चतुर्द्दश्यां विशेषेण ते यास्यंति परां गतिम् .. 104 ..
14.29.m: Dharma said: / 'Those who perform a ritual ablution here in this exceedingly sacred, auspicious water, / especially on the fourteenth day, shall attain the supreme state.

14.29.s:
tava nāmnā supuṇyaṃ hi tīrthametadbhaviṣyati ..
darśamuddiśya martyastu prāpsyate gosahasrakam ..
snānāllakṣaguṇaṃ dānātpuṇyaṃ caiva tathā'kṣayam .. 105 ..
14.29.d:
तव नाम्ना सुपुण्यं हि तीर्थमेतद्भविष्यति ..
दर्शमुद्दिश्य मर्त्यस्तु प्राप्स्यते गोसहस्रकम् ..
स्नानाल्लक्षगुणं दानात्पुण्यं चैव तथाऽक्षयम् .. 105 ..
14.29.m: Indeed, this shall be a very sacred ford by your name. / By making an offering on the new moon day, a mortal shall obtain [the fruit of giving] a thousand cows; / the merit from ritual ablution is multiplied a hundred thousand times, and from a gift it is imperishable.

14.29.s:
ye'tra śrāddhaṃ kariṣyaṃti mānavāḥ susamāhitāḥ..
sarvadānaphalaṃ teṣāṃ bhuktimuktī mahātmanām .. 106 ..
14.29.d:
येऽत्र श्राद्धं करिष्यंति मानवाः सुसमाहिताः..
सर्वदानफलं तेषां भुक्तिमुक्ती महात्मनाम् .. 106 ..
14.29.m: Those men who, well-composed, perform a śrāddha here— / for those noble-minded ones, there is the fruit of all gifts, worldly enjoyment, and liberation.

14.29.s:
api kīṭapataṃgā ye tṛṣārtāḥ salile śubhe ..
majjayiṣyati yāsyaṃti te'pi sthānaṃ divaukasām.. 107 ..
14.29.d:
अपि कीटपतंगा ये तृषार्ताः सलिले शुभे ..
मज्जयिष्यति यास्यंति तेऽपि स्थानं दिवौकसाम्.. 107 ..
14.29.m: Even worms and insects, afflicted by thirst, who plunge / into this auspicious water, shall also go to the abode of the gods.

14.29.s:
kiṃ punarbhaktisaṃyuktā mānavāḥ satyavādinaḥ ..
manasvino mahābhāgāḥ śraddhāvaṃto vicakṣaṇāḥ .. 108 ..
14.29.d:
किं पुनर्भक्तिसंयुक्ता मानवाः सत्यवादिनः ..
मनस्विनो महाभागाः श्रद्धावंतो विचक्षणाः .. 108 ..
14.29.m: What then of truthful human beings endowed with devotion, / wise, fortunate, faithful, and discerning?'

14.29.s:
.. pulastya uvāca .. ..
etasminneva kāle tu vimānāni sahasraśaḥ ..
samāyātāni rājeṃdra kapilāyāḥ prabhāvataḥ .. 109 ..
14.29.d:
.. पुलस्त्य उवाच .. ..
एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु विमानानि सहस्रशः ..
समायातानि राजेंद्र कपिलायाः प्रभावतः .. 109 ..
14.29.m: Pulastya said: / At that very moment, aerial chariots by the thousands / arrived, O king of kings, by the power of Kapilā.

14.29.s:
tānyāruhyātha kapilā gopagokulasaṃkulā ..
suprabheṇa samāyuktā tatpadaṃ paramaṃ gatā .. 7.3.29.110 ..
14.29.d:
तान्यारुह्याथ कपिला गोपगोकुलसंकुला ..
सुप्रभेण समायुक्ता तत्पदं परमं गता .. 7.3.29.110 ..
14.29.m: Mounting them, Kapilā, accompanied by cowherds and the herd of cattle, / and united with Suprabha, went to that supreme abode.

14.29.s:
tasmātsarvaprayatnena tatra snānaṃ samācaret ..
śrāddhaṃ caivātmanaḥ śaktyā dānaṃ pārthivasattama .. .. 111 ..
iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ saptame prabhāsakhaṃḍe tṛtīye'rbudakhaṃḍe kapilātīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃnāmaikonatriṃśo'dhyāyaḥ..29..
14.29.d:
तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन तत्र स्नानं समाचरेत् ..
श्राद्धं चैवात्मनः शक्त्या दानं पार्थिवसत्तम .. .. 111 ..
इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां सप्तमे प्रभासखंडे तृतीयेऽर्बुदखंडे कपिलातीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनंनामैकोनत्रिंशोऽध्यायः..29..
14.29.m:
Therefore, by every effort, one should perform a ritual ablution there, / and a śrāddha according to one's ability, and a gift, O best of kings.
Thus ends the twenty-ninth chapter, titled “Description of the Greatness of Kapilātīrtha,” in the third Arbudakhaṇḍa of the seventh Prabhāsakhaṇḍa in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand [verses].

14.30.s:
pulastya uvāca..
agnitīrthaṃ tato gacchetpāvanaṃ paramaṃ nṛṇām..
tatra vahniḥ purā naṣṭo labdhaśca tridaśairapi.. 1 ..
14.30.d:
पुलस्त्य उवाच..
अग्नितीर्थं ततो गच्छेत्पावनं परमं नृणाम्..
तत्र वह्निः पुरा नष्टो लब्धश्च त्रिदशैरपि.. 1 ..

14.30.s:
yayātiruvāca..
kimarthaṃ bhagavanvahniḥ purā naṣṭo dvijottama..
kathaṃ tatraiva labdhastu kautukaṃ me mahāmune..2..
14.30.d:
ययातिरुवाच..
किमर्थं भगवन्वह्निः पुरा नष्टो द्विजोत्तम..
कथं तत्रैव लब्धस्तु कौतुकं मे महामुने..2..
14.30.m:
Yayāti said:
For what reason, O venerable one, was Fire lost in ancient times, O best of the twice-born?
And how was he recovered right there? Great is my curiosity, O great sage!

14.30.s:
pulastya uvāca..
purā vṛṣṭinirodho'bhūdyāvaddvādaśavatsarān..
saṃśayaṃ paramaṃ prāptaḥ sarvo lokaḥ kṣudhārditaḥ .. 3 ..
14.30.d:
पुलस्त्य उवाच..
पुरा वृष्टिनिरोधोऽभूद्यावद्द्वादशवत्सरान्..
संशयं परमं प्राप्तः सर्वो लोकः क्षुधार्दितः .. 3 ..

14.30.s:
prāyo mṛto mṛtaprāyaḥ śeṣo'bhūddharaṇītale ..
naṣṭā araṇyajā grāmyāḥ paśavaḥ pakṣiṇo mṛgāḥ .. 4 ..
14.30.d:
प्रायो मृतो मृतप्रायः शेषोऽभूद्धरणीतले ..
नष्टा अरण्यजा ग्राम्याः पशवः पक्षिणो मृगाः .. 4 ..
14.30.m:
For the most part it was dead; what was left on the surface of the earth was almost dead;
wild and domestic animals, birds, and deer were destroyed.

14.30.s:
evaṃ kṛcchramanuprāpte martyaloke narādhipaḥ ..
viśvāmitro munivaraḥ saṃdehaṃ paramaṃ gataḥ .. 5 ..
14.30.d:
एवं कृच्छ्रमनुप्राप्ते मर्त्यलोके नराधिपः ..
विश्वामित्रो मुनिवरः संदेहं परमं गतः .. 5 ..
14.30.m:
When the mortal world had thus fallen into dire distress, O lord of men,
Viśvāmitra, the best of sages, fell into extreme uncertainty.

14.30.s:
annauṣadhirasābhāvādasthiśeṣo vyajāyata ..
anyasmindivase prāptaḥ kṣutkṣāmaḥ paryaṭandiśaḥ .. 6 ..
14.30.d:
अन्नौषधिरसाभावादस्थिशेषो व्यजायत ..
अन्यस्मिन्दिवसे प्राप्तः क्षुत्क्षामः पर्यटन्दिशः .. 6 ..
14.30.m:
Owing to the lack of food, herbs, and essence, he became reduced to mere bones;
on another day, emaciated by hunger, wandering through the directions,

14.30.s:
caṃḍālanilayaṃ prāptaḥ kṣuttṛṣāpīḍito bhṛśam ..
tatrāpaśyanmṛtaṃ śvānaṃ śuṣkaṃ pārthivasattama .. 7 ..
14.30.d:
चंडालनिलयं प्राप्तः क्षुत्तृषापीडितो भृशम् ..
तत्रापश्यन्मृतं श्वानं शुष्कं पार्थिवसत्तम .. 7 ..
14.30.m:
tormented greatly by hunger and thirst, he reached the dwelling of a Caṇḍāla.
There he saw a dead, dried dog, O best of kings.

14.30.s:
tamādāya gṛhaṃ prāptaḥ prakṣālya salilena tu ..
kṣutkṣāmaḥ pācayāmāsa tatastaṃ pāvake'juhot .. 8 ..
14.30.d:
तमादाय गृहं प्राप्तः प्रक्षाल्य सलिलेन तु ..
क्षुत्क्षामः पाचयामास ततस्तं पावकेऽजुहोत् .. 8 ..
14.30.m:
Taking it, he reached home, washed it with water,
and emaciated by hunger, cooked it; then he offered it into the fire.

14.30.s:
abhakṣyabhakṣaṇaṃ jñātvā havyavāhastato nṛpa ..
śakrasyopari manyuṃ svaṃ cakre'tīva mahīpate .. 9 ..
14.30.d:
अभक्ष्यभक्षणं ज्ञात्वा हव्यवाहस्ततो नृप ..
शक्रस्योपरि मन्युं स्वं चक्रेऽतीव महीपते .. 9 ..
14.30.m:
Knowing that uneatable food was being eaten, the fire-god, O king,
then conceived violent anger against Śakra, O lord of the earth:

14.30.s:
naṣṭauṣadhirase loke yuktametaddhi sāṃpratam ..
yādṛgāptaṃ havistādṛgagnibhakṣo viśiṣyate .. 7.3.30.10 ..
14.30.d:
नष्टौषधिरसे लोके युक्तमेतद्धि सांप्रतम् ..
यादृगाप्तं हविस्तादृगग्निभक्षो विशिष्यते .. 7.3.30.10 ..
14.30.m:
“In a world where the essence of herbs is lost, this is indeed fitting now;
whatever oblation has been obtained, such becomes the food of Fire!

14.30.s:
nābhakṣyaṃ bhakṣayiṣyāmi tyajiṣye kṣitimaṃḍalam ..
yena śakrādayo devā yāṃti kaṣṭatarāṃ daśām.. 11 ..
14.30.d:
नाभक्ष्यं भक्षयिष्यामि त्यजिष्ये क्षितिमंडलम् ..
येन शक्रादयो देवा यांति कष्टतरां दशाम्.. 11 ..
14.30.m:
I will not consume what is uneatable; I shall abandon the orb of the earth,
so that the gods headed by Śakra will go to an even more wretched state.”

14.30.s:
evaṃ saṃciṃtya manasā sakopo havyavāhanaḥ ..
praṇaṣṭaḥ sakalaṃ hitvā martyalokaṃ carācaram .. 12 ..
14.30.d:
एवं संचिंत्य मनसा सकोपो हव्यवाहनः ..
प्रणष्टः सकलं हित्वा मर्त्यलोकं चराचरम् .. 12 ..
14.30.m:
Having thus reflected in his mind, the fire-god, filled with wrath,
vanished, leaving behind the entire mortal world, moving and unmoving.

14.30.s:
praṇaṣṭe sahasā vahnāvagniṣṭomādikāḥ kriyāḥ ..
praṇaṣṭāstu janāḥ sarve viśeṣātsaṃśayaṃ gatāḥ .. 13 ..
14.30.d:
प्रणष्टे सहसा वह्नावग्निष्टोमादिकाः क्रियाः ..
प्रणष्टास्तु जनाः सर्वे विशेषात्संशयं गताः .. 13 ..
14.30.m:
When Fire had suddenly disappeared, rites such as the Agniṣṭoma were discontinued;
all people were ruined and fell into utter distress.

14.30.s:
tato devagaṇāḥ sarve saṃdehaṃ paramaṃ gatāḥ ..
yajñabhāgavihīnatvānmaṃtraṃ cakrustato mithaḥ .. 14 ..
14.30.d:
ततो देवगणाः सर्वे संदेहं परमं गताः ..
यज्ञभागविहीनत्वान्मंत्रं चक्रुस्ततो मिथः .. 14 ..
14.30.m:
Then all the hosts of gods fell into extreme uncertainty;
being deprived of their sacrificial shares, they then took counsel among themselves:

14.30.s:
tyaktastu vahninā martyastato nāśaṃ gatā narāḥ ..
śeṣanāśādvayaṃ sarve vinaṃkṣyāmo na saṃśayaḥ .. 15 ..
14.30.d:
त्यक्तस्तु वह्निना मर्त्यस्ततो नाशं गता नराः ..
शेषनाशाद्वयं सर्वे विनंक्ष्यामो न संशयः .. 15 ..
14.30.m:
“Mortal [existence] has been abandoned by Fire, and therefore men have perished;
by the destruction of the remainder, all of us will perish, there is no doubt.

14.30.s:
tasmādanveṣyatāṃ vahniryatra tiṣṭhati sāṃpratam ..
yathā carati martye ca tathā nītirvidhīyatām.. 16 ..
14.30.d:
तस्मादन्वेष्यतां वह्निर्यत्र तिष्ठति सांप्रतम् ..
यथा चरति मर्त्ये च तथा नीतिर्विधीयताम्.. 16 ..
14.30.m:
Therefore let Fire be searched for, wherever he now stays;
and let such policy be ordained so that he may move among mortals again.”

14.30.s:
.. pulastya uvāca .. ..
evaṃ te niścayaṃ kṛtvā sarve devāḥ savāsavāḥ ..
anvaiṣayaṃstathāgniṃ te samaṃtātkṣitimaṃḍale .. 17 ..
14.30.d:
.. पुलस्त्य उवाच .. ..
एवं ते निश्चयं कृत्वा सर्वे देवाः सवासवाः ..
अन्वैषयंस्तथाग्निं ते समंतात्क्षितिमंडले .. 17 ..
14.30.m:
Pulastya said:
Having thus made their resolve, all the gods along with Indra
searched for Fire all around the orb of the earth.

14.30.s:
tataste purato dṛṣṭvā śukaṃ śrāṃtā divaukasaḥ ..
papracchuḥ śraddhayā vahniryadi dṛṣṭaḥ prakathyatām ..18..
14.30.d:
ततस्ते पुरतो दृष्ट्वा शुकं श्रांता दिवौकसः ..
पप्रच्छुः श्रद्धया वह्निर्यदि दृष्टः प्रकथ्यताम् ..18..
14.30.m:
Then the exhausted denizens of heaven, seeing a parrot before them,
asked with faith: “If Fire has been seen, let it be told.”

14.30.s:
.. śuka uvāca .. ..
yo'yaṃ vaṃśo mahānagre pradagdho vahnisaṃgataḥ ..
praṇaṣṭo havyavāhotra mayā dṛṣṭo mahādyutiḥ .. 19 ..
14.30.d:
.. शुक उवाच .. ..
योऽयं वंशो महानग्रे प्रदग्धो वह्निसंगतः ..
प्रणष्टो हव्यवाहोत्र मया दृष्टो महाद्युतिः .. 19 ..
14.30.m:
The parrot said:
“That great bamboo which was burnt in front, in contact with fire—
there the fire-god of great splendor vanished; he was seen by me.”

14.30.s:
śukenāvedito vahniḥ śaptvā taṃ manyunā vṛtaḥ ..
gadgadā bhāvi te vāṇī proktvedaṃ prasthito drutam .. 7.3.30.20 ..
14.30.d:
शुकेनावेदितो वह्निः शप्त्वा तं मन्युना वृतः ..
गद्गदा भावि ते वाणी प्रोक्त्वेदं प्रस्थितो द्रुतम् .. 7.3.30.20 ..
14.30.m:
Betrayed by the parrot, Fire, filled with wrath, cursed him:
“Your voice shall become stammering!” Having said this, he quickly departed.

14.30.s:
praviveśa śamīgarbhamaśvatthaṃ tarusattamam ..
tatrastho dviparājñā sa kathito vibudhānprati .. 21 ..
14.30.d:
प्रविवेश शमीगर्भमश्वत्थं तरुसत्तमम् ..
तत्रस्थो द्विपराज्ञा स कथितो विबुधान्प्रति .. 21 ..
14.30.m:
He entered the hollow of a śamī tree and an aśvattha, the best of trees;
standing there, he was told to the gods by the king of elephants.

14.30.s:
sa taṃ provāca te jihvā viparītā bhaviṣyati ..
tato jalāśayaṃ gatvā parvate'rbudasaṃjñake .. 22 ..
14.30.d:
स तं प्रोवाच ते जिह्वा विपरीता भविष्यति ..
ततो जलाशयं गत्वा पर्वतेऽर्बुदसंज्ञके .. 22 ..
14.30.m:
He said to him: “Your tongue shall become inverted!”
Then, having gone to a body of water on the mountain named Arbuda,

14.30.s:
praviṣṭo bhagavānvahniryathā devairna lakṣyate ..
tatrotthena dardureṇa teṣāṃ prokto hutāśanaḥ .. 23 ..
14.30.d:
प्रविष्टो भगवान्वह्निर्यथा देवैर्न लक्ष्यते ..
तत्रोत्थेन दर्दुरेण तेषां प्रोक्तो हुताशनः .. 23 ..
14.30.m:
the venerable Fire entered so that he would not be noticed by the gods;
by a frog that rose up there, the Fire was reported to them:

14.30.s:
atrā'sau tiṣṭhate vahnirnirjhare parvatasya ca ..
dagdhāśca jalajāḥ sarve sutaptenaiva vāriṇā .. .. 24 ..
14.30.d:
अत्राऽसौ तिष्ठते वह्निर्निर्झरे पर्वतस्य च ..
दग्धाश्च जलजाः सर्वे सुतप्तेनैव वारिणा .. .. 24 ..
14.30.m:
“Here stays this Fire, in the mountain's waterfall;
and all water-born creatures have been burnt by the thoroughly boiling water.

14.30.s:
kṛcchrādahaṃ viniṣkrāṃtastasmānmṛtyumukhātsurāḥ ..
tacchrutvā yatnamāsthāya praviṣṭo havyavāhanaḥ .. 25 ..
14.30.d:
कृच्छ्रादहं विनिष्क्रांतस्तस्मान्मृत्युमुखात्सुराः ..
तच्छ्रुत्वा यत्नमास्थाय प्रविष्टो हव्यवाहनः .. 25 ..
14.30.m:
With difficulty have I escaped from that mouth of death, O gods!”
Hearing that, Fire, having made an effort, entered [deep within].

14.30.s: bhaviṣyasi vijihvastvaṃ śaptvā taṃ darduraṃ nṛpaḥ .. 26 ..
14.30.d: भविष्यसि विजिह्वस्त्वं शप्त्वा तं दर्दुरं नृपः .. 26 ..
14.30.m: “You shall become tongueless!” cursed he the frog, O king.

14.30.s:
tato devagaṇāḥ sarve niṣkrāṃtāḥ salilāśrayāt ..
saṃveṣṭya tuṣṭuvuḥ sarve stavairvedodbhavairnṛpa .. 27 ..
14.30.d:
ततो देवगणाः सर्वे निष्क्रांताः सलिलाश्रयात् ..
संवेष्ट्य तुष्टुवुः सर्वे स्तवैर्वेदोद्भवैर्नृप .. 27 ..
14.30.m:
Then all the hosts of gods, emerging from the shelter of the water,
surrounded him and all praised him with hymns born of the Vedas, O king.

14.30.s:
.. devā ūcuḥ .. ..
tvamagne sarvabhūtānāmaṃtaścarasi pāvaka ..
tvayā hīnaṃ jagatsarvaṃ nāśaṃ yāsyati satvaram .. 28 ..
14.30.d:
.. देवा ऊचुः .. ..
त्वमग्ने सर्वभूतानामंतश्चरसि पावक ..
त्वया हीनं जगत्सर्वं नाशं यास्यति सत्वरम् .. 28 ..

14.30.s:
tvaṃ mukhaṃ sarvadevānāṃ tvayi lokāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ ..
bhūloke ca tvayā tyakte vayaṃ sarve savāsavāḥ ..
vināśameva yāsyāmastasmāttvaṃ trātumarhasi .. 29 ..
14.30.d:
त्वं मुखं सर्वदेवानां त्वयि लोकाः प्रतिष्ठिताः ..
भूलोके च त्वया त्यक्ते वयं सर्वे सवासवाः ..
विनाशमेव यास्यामस्तस्मात्त्वं त्रातुमर्हसि .. 29 ..

14.30.s:
tvaṃ brahmā tvaṃ mahādevastvaṃ viṣṇustvaṃ divākaraḥ ..
tvaṃ caṃdrastvaṃ ca dhanado maruttvaṃ ca sureśvaraḥ ..7.3.30.30..
14.30.d:
त्वं ब्रह्मा त्वं महादेवस्त्वं विष्णुस्त्वं दिवाकरः ..
त्वं चंद्रस्त्वं च धनदो मरुत्त्वं च सुरेश्वरः ..7.3.30.30..
14.30.m:
You are Brahmā, you are Mahādeva, you are Viṣṇu, you are the sun,
you are the moon, and you are the giver of wealth, the wind, and the lord of the gods.

14.30.s:
iṃdrādyā vibudhāḥ sarve tvadāyattā hutāśana ..
kimarthaṃ bhagavanmarttyaṃ tyaktvā tvamatra saṃsthitaḥ ..
kimarthaṃ bhagavannasmānanāgāṃstyaktumicchasi .. 31 ..
14.30.d:
इंद्राद्या विबुधाः सर्वे त्वदायत्ता हुताशन ..
किमर्थं भगवन्मर्त्त्यं त्यक्त्वा त्वमत्र संस्थितः ..
किमर्थं भगवन्नस्माननागांस्त्यक्तुमिच्छसि .. 31 ..

14.30.s:
.. pulastya uvāca .. ..
veṣṭito bhagavānvahnirdevaiḥ stutiparāyaṇaiḥ ..
tasyaiva nirjharasyātha taṭastho vākyamabravīt .. 32 ..
14.30.d:
.. पुलस्त्य उवाच .. ..
वेष्टितो भगवान्वह्निर्देवैः स्तुतिपरायणैः ..
तस्यैव निर्झरस्याथ तटस्थो वाक्यमब्रवीत् .. 32 ..
14.30.m:
Pulastya said:
Surrounded by the gods intent upon praise,
the venerable Fire, standing on the bank of that very waterfall, then spoke these words:

14.30.s:
.. vahniruvāca .. ..
abhakṣyabhakṣaṇe śakro māmicchati niyojitum ..
tenaiva na karotyeṣa vṛṣṭiṃ marttye sureśvaraḥ .. 33 ..
14.30.d:
.. वह्निरुवाच .. ..
अभक्ष्यभक्षणे शक्रो मामिच्छति नियोजितुम् ..
तेनैव न करोत्येष वृष्टिं मर्त्त्ये सुरेश्वरः .. 33 ..

14.30.s:
ato'haṃ bhūtalaṃ tyaktvā praviṣṭo nirjhare tviha ..
praṇaṣṭānnarase loke na cāhaṃ sthātumutsahe .. 34 ..
14.30.d:
अतोऽहं भूतलं त्यक्त्वा प्रविष्टो निर्झरे त्विह ..
प्रणष्टान्नरसे लोके न चाहं स्थातुमुत्सहे .. 34 ..
14.30.m:
Therefore, having abandoned the surface of the earth, I have entered here into the waterfall;
and in a world where the essence of food is ruined, I have no desire to stay.

14.30.s:
.. śakra uvāca .. ..
śṛṇu yasmānmayā rodhaḥ kṛto vṛṣṭerhutāśana ..
devāpirnāma dharmajñaḥ kṣatriyāṇāṃ yaśaskaraḥ .. 35 ..
14.30.d:
.. शक्र उवाच .. ..
शृणु यस्मान्मया रोधः कृतो वृष्टेर्हुताशन ..
देवापिर्नाम धर्मज्ञः क्षत्रियाणां यशस्करः .. 35 ..
14.30.m:
Śakra said:
Hear, O Fire, why the obstruction of rain was made by me:
there was a knower of dharma named Devāpi, who brought fame to the kṣatriyas.

14.30.s:
pratīpastatsutaḥ sādhuḥ sarvaśīlavatāṃ varaḥ ..
devāpau ca gate svargaṃ jyeṣṭhabhrātaramagrajam..
saṃtyaktvā jagṛhe rājyaṃ śaṃtanustatsuto'varaḥ .. 36 ..
14.30.d:
प्रतीपस्तत्सुतः साधुः सर्वशीलवतां वरः ..
देवापौ च गते स्वर्गं ज्येष्ठभ्रातरमग्रजम्..
संत्यक्त्वा जगृहे राज्यं शंतनुस्तत्सुतोऽवरः .. 36 ..

14.30.s:
etasmātkāraṇādrājye tasya vṛṣṭirnirākṛtā ..
tavādeśātkariṣyāmi nivartasva hutāśana .. 37 ..
14.30.d:
एतस्मात्कारणाद्राज्ये तस्य वृष्टिर्निराकृता ..
तवादेशात्करिष्यामि निवर्तस्व हुताशन .. 37 ..
14.30.m:
For this reason, rain was withheld in his kingdom.
At your command I shall make [it rain]; turn back, O Fire!

14.30.s:
.. pulastya uvāca .. ..
evamuktvā sahasrākṣaḥ puṣkarāvartakānghanān ..
drutamājñāpayāmāsa vṛṣṭyarthaṃ jagatītale.. 38..
14.30.d:
.. पुलस्त्य उवाच .. ..
एवमुक्त्वा सहस्राक्षः पुष्करावर्तकान्घनान् ..
द्रुतमाज्ञापयामास वृष्ट्यर्थं जगतीतले.. 38..
14.30.m:
Pulastya said:
Having spoken thus, the thousand-eyed Indra quickly commanded
the Puṣkarāvarta clouds to rain upon the surface of the earth.

14.30.s:
atha śakrasamādiṣṭā vidyutvanto balāhakāḥ..
gambhīrarāviṇaḥ sarvaṃ bhūtalaṃ pracurairjalaiḥ..
pūrayāmāsuratyugrā dyutimanto mahīpate.. 39..
14.30.d:
अथ शक्रसमादिष्टा विद्युत्वन्तो बलाहकाः..
गम्भीरराविणः सर्वं भूतलं प्रचुरैर्जलैः..
पूरयामासुरत्युग्रा द्युतिमन्तो महीपते.. 39..
14.30.m:
Then, commanded by Śakra, the lightning-bearing clouds,
deep-thundering, highly fierce, and resplendent, filled the entire
surface of the earth with abundant waters, O lord of the earth.

14.30.s:
tato'gamatparāṃ tuṣṭiṃ bhagavānhavyavāhanaḥ..
rocayāmāsa bhūpṛṣṭhe vasatiṃ devakāraṇāt.. 7.3.30.40..
14.30.d:
ततोऽगमत्परां तुष्टिं भगवान्हव्यवाहनः..
रोचयामास भूपृष्ठे वसतिं देवकारणात्.. 7.3.30.40..
14.30.m: Then the blessed Carrier of Oblations attained supreme satisfaction; / he was pleased to reside on the surface of the earth for the sake of the gods.

14.30.s:
devā ūcuḥ..
tavā''deśātkṛtā vṛṣṭiranyatkāryaṃ hutāśana ..
yatte priyaṃ tadasmākaṃ suśīghraṃ hi nivedaya .. 41 ..
14.30.d:
देवा ऊचुः..
तवा'ऽदेशात्कृता वृष्टिरन्यत्कार्यं हुताशन ..
यत्ते प्रियं तदस्माकं सुशीघ्रं हि निवेदय .. 41 ..
14.30.m: The gods said: / 'By your command rain has been made; what other task is there, O Fire, / that is pleasing to you? Declare that to us very quickly indeed.'

14.30.s:
.. agniruvāca .. ..
etajjalāśayaṃ puṇyaṃ mannāmnā tīrthamuttamam ..
khyātiṃ yātu dharāpṛṣṭhe yuṣmākaṃ hi prasādataḥ .. 42 ..
14.30.d:
.. अग्निरुवाच .. ..
एतज्जलाशयं पुण्यं मन्नाम्ना तीर्थमुत्तमम् ..
ख्यातिं यातु धरापृष्ठे युष्माकं हि प्रसादतः .. 42 ..
14.30.m: Agni said: / 'Through your grace, may this holy pool of water, an excellent sacred ford in my name, / attain fame on the surface of the earth.'

14.30.s:
.. devā ūcuḥ .. ..
agnitīrthamidaṃ loke prakhyātiṃ saṃprayāsyati ..
atra snāto naraḥ samyagagnilokaṃ prayāsyati .. 43 ..
14.30.d:
.. देवा ऊचुः .. ..
अग्नितीर्थमिदं लोके प्रख्यातिं संप्रयास्यति ..
अत्र स्नातो नरः सम्यगग्निलोकं प्रयास्यति .. 43 ..
14.30.m: The gods said: / 'This Agnitīrtha shall attain renown in the world; / a person having performed a ritual ablution here properly shall go to the world of Agni.

14.30.s:
yastilāndāsyati narastīrthe'sminsusamāhitaḥ ..
agniṣṭomasya yajñasya phalaṃ tasya bhaviṣyati ..44..
14.30.d:
यस्तिलान्दास्यति नरस्तीर्थेऽस्मिन्सुसमाहितः ..
अग्निष्टोमस्य यज्ञस्य फलं तस्य भविष्यति ..44..
14.30.m: A person who, deeply concentrated, shall give sesamum seeds at this sacred ford, / shall attain the fruit of an Agniṣṭoma sacrifice.'

14.30.s:
.. pulastya uvāca .. ..
evamuktvā surāḥ sarve svasvasthānaṃ yayustataḥ ..
vahniśca bhagavānrājanyathāpūrvamavartata .. 45 ..
14.30.d:
.. पुलस्त्य उवाच .. ..
एवमुक्त्वा सुराः सर्वे स्वस्वस्थानं ययुस्ततः ..
वह्निश्च भगवान्राजन्यथापूर्वमवर्तत .. 45 ..
14.30.m: Pulastya said: / Having spoken thus, all the gods then went to their respective abodes; / and the blessed fire, O king, remained as before.

14.30.s: yaścaitpaṭhate nityaṃ prātarutthāya cottamam .. agnitīrthasya māhātmyaṃ mucyate sarvapātakaiḥ .. 46 ..
14.30.d: यश्चैत्पठते नित्यं प्रातरुत्थाय चोत्तमम् .. अग्नितीर्थस्य माहात्म्यं मुच्यते सर्वपातकैः .. 46 ..
14.30.m: And whoever, rising in the morning, constantly recites this excellent / māhātmya of Agnitīrtha, is freed from all sins.

14.30.s:
ahorātrakṛtātpāpātsa śṛṇvannapi mucyate .. 47 ..
iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekā śītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ saptame prabhāsakhaṃḍe tṛtīye'rbudakhaṇḍe'gnitīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃnāma triṃśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 30 ..
14.30.d:
अहोरात्रकृतात्पापात्स शृण्वन्नपि मुच्यते .. 47 ..
इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एका शीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां सप्तमे प्रभासखंडे तृतीयेऽर्बुदखण्डेऽग्नितीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनंनाम त्रिंशोऽध्यायः .. 30 ..
14.30.m:
Even while merely hearing it, he is freed from the sin committed by day and night.
Thus ends the thirtieth chapter, named 'Description of the Māhātmya of Agnitīrtha', in the Arbuda section, the third [part] of the seventh [book], the Prabhāsakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Purāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand [verses].

14.31.s:
.. pulastya uvāca .. ..
raktānubandhaṃ vai gacchettīrthaṃ trailokyaviśrutam ..
yatra snāto naraḥ samyaṅmucyate brahmahatyayā .. 1 ..
14.31.d:
.. पुलस्त्य उवाच .. ..
रक्तानुबन्धं वै गच्छेत्तीर्थं त्रैलोक्यविश्रुतम् ..
यत्र स्नातो नरः सम्यङ्मुच्यते ब्रह्महत्यया .. 1 ..
14.31.m: Pulastya said: / One should go to Raktānubandha, a sacred ford renowned throughout the three worlds, / bathed in which a person is properly freed from [the sin of] killing a brahmin.

14.31.s:
purā''sītpārthivonāma iṃdraseno mahīpatiḥ ..
tasyā''sītsupriyā bhāryā sunandānāma bhāminī ..
pativratā patiprāṇā sadā patyuḥ priye sthitā .. 2 ..
14.31.d:
पुरा'ऽसीत्पार्थिवोनाम इंद्रसेनो महीपतिः ..
तस्या'ऽसीत्सुप्रिया भार्या सुनन्दानाम भामिनी ..
पतिव्रता पतिप्राणा सदा पत्युः प्रिये स्थिता .. 2 ..
14.31.m: Formerly there was an earthly king named Indrasena; / he had a very beloved wife, a lovely woman named Sunandā, / devoted to her husband, holding her husband as her life-breath, always intent on her husband's pleasure.

14.31.s:
kasyacittvatha kālasya sa rājā saparigrahaḥ ..
paradeśaṃ gato haṃtuṃ śatrusaṃghaṃ durāsadam .. 3 ..
14.31.d:
कस्यचित्त्वथ कालस्य स राजा सपरिग्रहः ..
परदेशं गतो हंतुं शत्रुसंघं दुरासदम् .. 3 ..
14.31.m: Now, at a certain time, that king with his retinue / went to a foreign land to slay a host of foes difficult to approach.

14.31.s:
taṃ nihatya dhanaṃ bhūri gṛhītvā prasthito gṛham ..
tato'gre preṣayāmāsa sa dūtaṃ kṛtrimaṃ nṛpa .. 4 ..
14.31.d:
तं निहत्य धनं भूरि गृहीत्वा प्रस्थितो गृहम् ..
ततोऽग्रे प्रेषयामास स दूतं कृत्रिमं नृप .. 4 ..
14.31.m: Having slain them and taken abundant wealth, he set out for home; / then, O king, he sent a deceptive messenger ahead, [saying]:

14.31.s:
sunandāṃ brūhi gatvā tvamindraseno hato raṇe ..
tadākārastato lakṣyaḥ pātivratye mamājñayā .. 5 ..
14.31.d:
सुनन्दां ब्रूहि गत्वा त्वमिन्द्रसेनो हतो रणे ..
तदाकारस्ततो लक्ष्यः पातिव्रत्ये ममाज्ञया .. 5 ..
14.31.m: 'Having gone, say to Sunandā: "Indrasena has been killed in battle"; / then, by my command, her demeanor regarding her devotion to her husband is to be observed.

14.31.s:
yadi sā niścayaṃ gacchenmaraṇaṃ prati bhāminī ..
tadā rakṣyā prayatnena vācyaṃ hāsyaṃ mamodbhavam .. 6 ..
14.31.d:
यदि सा निश्चयं गच्छेन्मरणं प्रति भामिनी ..
तदा रक्ष्या प्रयत्नेन वाच्यं हास्यं ममोद्भवम् .. 6 ..
14.31.m: If that lovely woman should form a resolve toward death, / then she is to be protected with effort, and my joke is to be spoken.'

14.31.s:
evamukto gato dūtastatkṣaṇānnṛpasattama ..
tasyai nivedadāmāsa yaduktaṃ tena bhūbhujā .. 7 ..
14.31.d:
एवमुक्तो गतो दूतस्तत्क्षणान्नृपसत्तम ..
तस्यै निवेददामास यदुक्तं तेन भूभुजा .. 7 ..
14.31.m: Having been spoken to thus, the messenger went at that very moment, O best of kings, / and announced to her what had been said by that king.

14.31.s:
atha tasya vacaḥ śrutvā sunaṃdā cāruhāsinī ..
gataprāṇā nṛpaśreṣṭha patiprāṇā mahāsatī .. 8 ..
14.31.d:
अथ तस्य वचः श्रुत्वा सुनंदा चारुहासिनी ..
गतप्राणा नृपश्रेष्ठ पतिप्राणा महासती .. 8 ..
14.31.m: Then, having heard his word, Sunandā of sweet smile, / holding her husband as her life-breath, a great chaste wife, departed this life, O best of kings.

14.31.s:
yasminkāle mṛtā sā tu sunandā śīlamaṃḍanā ..
tasminkāle nṛpaḥ so'pi tatpāpena samāśritaḥ .. 9 ..
14.31.d:
यस्मिन्काले मृता सा तु सुनन्दा शीलमंडना ..
तस्मिन्काले नृपः सोऽपि तत्पापेन समाश्रितः .. 9 ..
14.31.m: At that very time when that Sunandā, whose ornament was good conduct, died, / at that time that king too was overtaken by that sin.

14.31.s:
athāpaśyaddvitīyāṃ sa cchāyāṃ gātrasya copari ..
tathā gurutaraṃ kāyaṃ sālasyaṃ samapadyata .. 7.3.31.10 ..
14.31.d:
अथापश्यद्द्वितीयां स च्छायां गात्रस्य चोपरि ..
तथा गुरुतरं कायं सालस्यं समपद्यत .. 7.3.31.10 ..
14.31.m: Then he saw a second shadow over his body, / and his body became heavier, accompanied by lethargy,

14.31.s:
tejohīnaṃ sudurgaṃdhi vivarṇaṃ nṛpasattama ..
atha prāpto gṛhaṃ rājā śrutvā bhāryāsamudbhavam .. 11 ..
14.31.d:
तेजोहीनं सुदुर्गंधि विवर्णं नृपसत्तम ..
अथ प्राप्तो गृहं राजा श्रुत्वा भार्यासमुद्भवम् .. 11 ..
14.31.m: devoid of radiance, foul-smelling, and discolored, O best of kings. / Then the king arrived home, and having heard of the destruction

14.31.s:
vināśaṃ duḥkhaśokārtaḥ karuṇaṃ paryadevayat..
sa jñātvā pāpamātmānaṃ strīhatyāsuvidūṣitam.. 12 ..
14.31.d:
विनाशं दुःखशोकार्तः करुणं पर्यदेवयत्..
स ज्ञात्वा पापमात्मानं स्त्रीहत्यासुविदूषितम्.. 12 ..
14.31.m: that had befallen his wife, afflicted with grief and sorrow, he wailed piteously. / Knowing himself to be a sinner thoroughly defiled by the murder of a woman,

14.31.s:
brāhmaṇānāṃ samādeśāttathā yātrāparo'bhavat ..
kṛtvaurddhvadaihikaṃ tasyā laghumātra parigrahaḥ ..
vārāṇasyāṃ gataḥ pūrvaṃ tatra dānaṃ dadau bahu ..13..
14.31.d:
ब्राह्मणानां समादेशात्तथा यात्रापरोऽभवत् ..
कृत्वौर्द्ध्वदैहिकं तस्या लघुमात्र परिग्रहः ..
वाराणस्यां गतः पूर्वं तत्र दानं ददौ बहु ..13..
14.31.m: by the instruction of brahmins he then became intent on pilgrimage; / having performed her funeral rites with only minimal retinue, / he went first to Vārāṇasī and there gave abundant gifts

14.31.s:
kapālamocane tīrthe sarvapāpapraṇāśane ..
trinetro yatra nirmuktaḥ purā vai brahmahatyayā ..14..
14.31.d:
कपालमोचने तीर्थे सर्वपापप्रणाशने ..
त्रिनेत्रो यत्र निर्मुक्तः पुरा वै ब्रह्महत्यया ..14..
14.31.m: at Kapālamocana sacred ford, which destroys all sins, / where the Three-Eyed One was formerly freed indeed from [the sin of] killing a brahmin.

14.31.s:
tasya cchāyā dvitīyā sā na naṣṭā tatra bhūpate ..
tataḥ kanakhalaṃ prāptaḥ supuṇyaṃ śuddhidaṃ nṛṇām .. 15 ..
14.31.d:
तस्य च्छाया द्वितीया सा न नष्टा तत्र भूपते ..
ततः कनखलं प्राप्तः सुपुण्यं शुद्धिदं नृणाम् .. 15 ..
14.31.m: That second shadow of his did not disappear there, O lord of the earth; / then he reached Kanakhala, which is very holy and confers purity upon mortals;

14.31.s:
tathaiva puṣkarāraṇyaṃ tasmādamarakaṇṭakam ..
kurukṣetraṃ tato rājanprāpto'sau nṛpasattamaḥ .. 16 ..
14.31.d:
तथैव पुष्करारण्यं तस्मादमरकण्टकम् ..
कुरुक्षेत्रं ततो राजन्प्राप्तोऽसौ नृपसत्तमः .. 16 ..
14.31.m: likewise the forest of Puṣkara, and from there Amarakaṇṭaka; / then, O king, that best of kings reached Kurukṣetra,

14.31.s:
prabhāsaṃ somatīrthaṃ ca tatastu kṛmijāṃgale ..
ekahaṃsaṃ tato rājanpuṇyapāriplavaṃ tataḥ .. 17 ..
14.31.d:
प्रभासं सोमतीर्थं च ततस्तु कृमिजांगले ..
एकहंसं ततो राजन्पुण्यपारिप्लवं ततः .. 17 ..
14.31.m: Prabhāsa, and Somatīrtha; and then in Kṛmi-jāṅgala, / Ekahaṃsa; then, O king, holy Pāriplava;

14.31.s:
rudrakoṭiṃ virūpākṣaṃ tataḥ paṃcanadaṃ nṛpa ..
evamādīni tīrthāni puṇyānyāyatanāni ca ..
paribhramanmahīpāla pariśrāṃto narādhipaḥ .. 18 ..
14.31.d:
रुद्रकोटिं विरूपाक्षं ततः पंचनदं नृप ..
एवमादीनि तीर्थानि पुण्यान्यायतनानि च ..
परिभ्रमन्महीपाल परिश्रांतो नराधिपः .. 18 ..
14.31.m: Rudrakoṭi, Virūpākṣa, and then Pañcanada, O king. / Wandering about these and other sacred fords and holy shrines, / O protector of the earth, the king became exhausted.

14.31.s:
tato varṣasahasrāṃte saṃprāpto'rbudaparvate ..
tatrāpaśyannarapatistīrthānyāyatanāni ca .. 19 ..
14.31.d:
ततो वर्षसहस्रांते संप्राप्तोऽर्बुदपर्वते ..
तत्रापश्यन्नरपतिस्तीर्थान्यायतनानि च .. 19 ..
14.31.m: Then, at the end of a thousand years, he arrived at Mount Arbuda; / there the lord of men saw sacred fords and shrines,

14.31.s:
tapasvisaṃghānvividhānbrāhmaṇānvedapāragān ..
dadau dānāni bahuśo brāhmaṇebhyo yadṛcchayā .. 7.3.31.20 ..
14.31.d:
तपस्विसंघान्विविधान्ब्राह्मणान्वेदपारगान् ..
ददौ दानानि बहुशो ब्राह्मणेभ्यो यदृच्छया .. 7.3.31.20 ..
14.31.m: various hosts of ascetics, and brahmins who had mastered the Vedas; / he gave abundant gifts spontaneously to the brahmins.

14.31.s:
prāpto raktānubaṃdhaṃ ca tīrthaṃ tatraiva parvate ..
tatra snāto viniṣkrāṃto yāvatpaśyati bhūmipaḥ .. 21 ..
14.31.d:
प्राप्तो रक्तानुबंधं च तीर्थं तत्रैव पर्वते ..
तत्र स्नातो विनिष्क्रांतो यावत्पश्यति भूमिपः .. 21 ..
14.31.m: And on that very mountain he reached the sacred ford Raktānubandha; / having bathed there, as soon as the ruler of the earth came out and looked,

14.31.s:
tāvanna dṛśyate cchāyā dvitīyā strīvadhodbhavā ..
laghutvaṃ sarvagātrāṇi saṃprāptāni mahīpate .. 22 ..
14.31.d:
तावन्न दृश्यते च्छाया द्वितीया स्त्रीवधोद्भवा ..
लघुत्वं सर्वगात्राणि संप्राप्तानि महीपते .. 22 ..
14.31.m: so soon that second shadow arising from the killing of a woman was seen no more; / all his limbs attained lightness, O lord of the earth,

14.31.s:
vigandhatā praṇaṣṭā ca tejovṛddhiḥ parābhavat ..
tato hṛṣṭamanā bhūtvā dattvā dānāni bhūriśaḥ ..
stūyamānaścaturdikṣu baṃdibhiḥ prasthito gṛham .. 23 ..
14.31.d:
विगन्धता प्रणष्टा च तेजोवृद्धिः पराभवत् ..
ततो हृष्टमना भूत्वा दत्त्वा दानानि भूरिशः ..
स्तूयमानश्चतुर्दिक्षु बंदिभिः प्रस्थितो गृहम् .. 23 ..
14.31.m: the foul smell vanished, and a supreme increase of radiance occurred. / Then, having become joyful at heart and given copious gifts, / being praised in the four directions by bards, he set out for home.

14.31.s:
tato raktānubaṃdhasya somātikramaṇaṃ nṛpa ..
yāvatkaroti rājendra tāvadasya punastathā ..24..
14.31.d:
ततो रक्तानुबंधस्य सोमातिक्रमणं नृप ..
यावत्करोति राजेन्द्र तावदस्य पुनस्तथा ..24..
14.31.m: Then, O king, as soon as the best of kings crossed the boundary / of Raktānubandha,

14.31.s:
sā cchāyā dṛśyate dehe dvitīyā nṛpasattama ..
sa eva gandho gātreṣu tejohāniśca sā nṛpa .. 25 ..
14.31.d:
सा च्छाया दृश्यते देहे द्वितीया नृपसत्तम ..
स एव गन्धो गात्रेषु तेजोहानिश्च सा नृप .. 25 ..
14.31.m: so soon that second shadow was seen on his body again, O best of kings; / that very same smell was on his limbs, and that loss of radiance, O king.

14.31.s:
tato duḥkhābhisaṃtapto gatastatraiva tatkṣaṇāt ..
raktabaṃdhamanuprāpto vipāpmā so'bhavatpunaḥ .. 26 ..
14.31.d:
ततो दुःखाभिसंतप्तो गतस्तत्रैव तत्क्षणात् ..
रक्तबंधमनुप्राप्तो विपाप्मा सोऽभवत्पुनः .. 26 ..
14.31.m: Then, burning with distress, he went back to that very place that moment; / having arrived back at Raktabandha, he became free from sin once again.

14.31.s:
sa jñātvā tīrthamāhātmyaṃ paraṃ pārthivasattamaḥ ..
tatra dārūṇi cāhṛtya citāṃ kṛtvā tato nṛpa ..
dānaṃ dattvā dvijāgrebhyaḥ praviṣṭo havyavāhanam .. 27 ..
14.31.d:
स ज्ञात्वा तीर्थमाहात्म्यं परं पार्थिवसत्तमः ..
तत्र दारूणि चाहृत्य चितां कृत्वा ततो नृप ..
दानं दत्त्वा द्विजाग्रेभ्यः प्रविष्टो हव्यवाहनम् .. 27 ..
14.31.m: Knowing the supreme māhātmya of the sacred ford, that best of kings / fetched firewood there, built a funeral pyre, O king, / gave gifts to the foremost twice-born, and entered the fire.

14.31.s:
tato vimānamāruhya parityajya kalevaram ..
divyamālyāṃbaradharaḥ śivalokamupāgamat .. 28 ..
14.31.d:
ततो विमानमारुह्य परित्यज्य कलेवरम् ..
दिव्यमाल्यांबरधरः शिवलोकमुपागमत् .. 28 ..
14.31.m: Then, having abandoned his bodily frame and ascended an aerial chariot, / wearing divine garlands and garments, he went to the world of Śiva.

14.31.s:
śivalokamanuprāpte tasminpārthivasattame ..
devarṣayastadā vākyamidamāhuḥ suvismayāt .. 29 ..
14.31.d:
शिवलोकमनुप्राप्ते तस्मिन्पार्थिवसत्तमे ..
देवर्षयस्तदा वाक्यमिदमाहुः सुविस्मयात् .. 29 ..
14.31.m: When that best of kings had arrived in the world of Śiva, / the divine seers then spoke this utterance in great wonder:

14.31.s:
tīrthebhyastu paraṃ tīrthamidaṃ vai pāvanaṃ param ..
indraseno hyataḥ pāpāttīrthasaṃgādvyamucyata .. 7.3.31.30 ..
14.31.d:
तीर्थेभ्यस्तु परं तीर्थमिदं वै पावनं परम् ..
इन्द्रसेनो ह्यतः पापात्तीर्थसंगाद्व्यमुच्यत .. 7.3.31.30 ..
14.31.m: 'This is indeed the supreme purifier, a sacred ford higher than [all other] sacred fords; / for from this contact with the sacred ford Indrasena was freed from sin.'

14.31.s:
tataḥ prabhṛti tattīrthaṃ khyātaṃ ca dharaṇītale ..
raktānāṃ prāṇināṃ yasmādanubandhaṃ karoti yat .. 31 ..
14.31.d:
ततः प्रभृति तत्तीर्थं ख्यातं च धरणीतले ..
रक्तानां प्राणिनां यस्मादनुबन्धं करोति यत् .. 31 ..
14.31.m: From that time forth, that sacred ford became renowned on the surface of the earth; / because it binds attached living beings,

14.31.s:
raktānubandhamityeva tasmāttatkīrttyate kṣitau ..
tatra santarpya vai devānyaḥ śrāddhaṃ kurute nṛpa .. 32 ..
14.31.d:
रक्तानुबन्धमित्येव तस्मात्तत्कीर्त्त्यते क्षितौ ..
तत्र सन्तर्प्य वै देवान्यः श्राद्धं कुरुते नृप .. 32 ..
14.31.m: therefore it is proclaimed on earth as Raktānubandha. / O king, one who, having gratified the gods there, performs a funeral offering,

14.31.s:
tatra saṃkramaṇe bhānoryaḥ snānaṃ kurute naraḥ ..
śraddhayā parayā yukto mucyate brahmahatyayā .. 33 ..
14.31.d:
तत्र संक्रमणे भानोर्यः स्नानं कुरुते नरः ..
श्रद्धया परया युक्तो मुच्यते ब्रह्महत्यया .. 33 ..
14.31.m: The man who bathes there at the transit of the sun, / endowed with supreme faith, is freed from the sin of killing a brahmin.

14.31.s:
pitṛkṣetre gayāyāṃ ca śrāddhaṃ yaḥ kurute naraḥ ..
gayāśrāddhasamaṃ prāhuḥ phalaṃ tasya maharṣayaḥ .. 34 ..
14.31.d:
पितृक्षेत्रे गयायां च श्राद्धं यः कुरुते नरः ..
गयाश्राद्धसमं प्राहुः फलं तस्य महर्षयः .. 34 ..
14.31.m: When a man offers an ancestral rite there or in Gayā, the sacred field of the ancestors, / great seers say the fruit is equal to an ancestral rite at Gayā.

14.31.s:
candrasūryoparāge vā godānaṃ nṛpasattama ..
yaḥ karoti narastatra sa kulānsapta tārayet .. 35 ..
iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ saptame prabhāsakhaṇḍe tṛtīye'rbudakhaṃḍe raktānubandhamāhātmyavarṇanaṃnāmaikatriṃśo'dhyāyaḥ .. .. 31 ..
14.31.d:
चन्द्रसूर्योपरागे वा गोदानं नृपसत्तम ..
यः करोति नरस्तत्र स कुलान्सप्त तारयेत् .. 35 ..
इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां सप्तमे प्रभासखण्डे तृतीयेऽर्बुदखंडे रक्तानुबन्धमाहात्म्यवर्णनंनामैकत्रिंशोऽध्यायः .. .. 31 ..
14.31.m:
Or on an eclipse of the moon or the sun, O best of kings, / the man who gives a cow there delivers seven generations.
Thus ends the thirty-first chapter, entitled “Description of the Greatness of Raktānubandha,” in the Arbuda Section, the third part of the Prabhāsa Section, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a collection of eighty-one thousand [verses].

14.32.s:
pulastya uvāca .. ..
mahāvināyakaṃ gacchettataḥ pārthivasattama ..
yasmindṛṣṭe nṛṇāṃ sadyo nirvighnatvaṃ prajāyate .. 1 .. ..
14.32.d:
पुलस्त्य उवाच .. ..
महाविनायकं गच्छेत्ततः पार्थिवसत्तम ..
यस्मिन्दृष्टे नृणां सद्यो निर्विघ्नत्वं प्रजायते .. 1 .. ..
14.32.m: Pulastya said: / Then one should go to Mahāvināyaka, O best of kings, / upon seeing whom freedom from obstacles immediately arises for men.

14.32.s:
.. yayātiruvāca .. ..
kathaṃ mahattvamagamatpūrvaṃ tatra vināyakaḥ ..
kasminkāle dvijaśreṣṭha sarvaṃ vistarato vada .. 2 .. ..
14.32.d:
.. ययातिरुवाच .. ..
कथं महत्त्वमगमत्पूर्वं तत्र विनायकः ..
कस्मिन्काले द्विजश्रेष्ठ सर्वं विस्तरतो वद .. 2 .. ..
14.32.m: Yayāti said: / How did Vināyaka formerly attain greatness there? / At what time, O best of the twice-born? Tell me everything in detail.

14.32.s:
pulastya uvāca .. ..
purodvarttanajaṃ lepaṃ gṛhītvā nṛpa pārvatī ..
vinodārthaṃ cakārātha bālakaṃ sukumārakam .. 3 ..
14.32.d:
पुलस्त्य उवाच .. ..
पुरोद्वर्त्तनजं लेपं गृहीत्वा नृप पार्वती ..
विनोदार्थं चकाराथ बालकं सुकुमारकम् .. 3 ..
14.32.m: Pulastya said: / Formerly, O king, Pārvatī took the paste born of her fragrant body-ointment / and, for diversion, made a delicate boy.

14.32.s:
lepābhāvācchirohīnaṃ śeṣāṃgāvayavaṃ nṛpa ..
yathoktaṃ nirmayitvā taṃ skandaṃ vākyamathābravīt .. 4 ..
14.32.d:
लेपाभावाच्छिरोहीनं शेषांगावयवं नृप ..
यथोक्तं निर्मयित्वा तं स्कन्दं वाक्यमथाब्रवीत् .. 4 ..
14.32.m: For lack of paste, he was headless, having all the other limbs and members, O king. / Having fashioned him as described, she then spoke to Skanda:

14.32.s:
lepamānaya bhadraṃ te śiro'rthaṃ skanda satvaram ..
yenāyaṃ putrako me syādbhrātā te paradurjayaḥ .. 5 ..
14.32.d:
लेपमानय भद्रं ते शिरोऽर्थं स्कन्द सत्वरम् ..
येनायं पुत्रको मे स्याद्भ्राता ते परदुर्जयः .. 5 ..
14.32.m: “Bring paste quickly for a head, Skanda, may good fortune be yours, / so that he may be my little son, and your brother, invincible to enemies!”

14.32.s:
tato gaurīsamādeśāllepālabdhau nṛpottama ..
mattaṃ gajavaraṃ dṛṣṭvā śirastasya samānayat .. 6 ..
14.32.d:
ततो गौरीसमादेशाल्लेपालब्धौ नृपोत्तम ..
मत्तं गजवरं दृष्ट्वा शिरस्तस्य समानयत् .. 6 ..
14.32.m: Then, by Gaurī's command, unable to find paste, O best of kings, / seeing an elephant in rut, he brought its head.

14.32.s:
tasminniyojayāmāsa gātre lepasamudbhave ..
mahaddhīdaṃ śiro bhāvi putra kasmāttvayā''hṛtam .. 7 ..
14.32.d:
तस्मिन्नियोजयामास गात्रे लेपसमुद्भवे ..
महद्धीदं शिरो भावि पुत्र कस्मात्त्वया'ऽहृतम् .. 7 ..
14.32.m: He affixed it onto that body born of the paste: / “Indeed, this head will be huge, my son! Why did you bring it?”

14.32.s:
bruvaṃtyāścāpi pārvatyā mā meti ca muhurmuhuḥ ..
nyaste śirasi tadgātre daivayogānnarādhipa .. 8 ..
14.32.d:
ब्रुवंत्याश्चापि पार्वत्या मा मेति च मुहुर्मुहुः ..
न्यस्ते शिरसि तद्गात्रे दैवयोगान्नराधिप .. 8 ..
14.32.m: Even while Pārvatī was crying, “No, no!” again and again, / the head was joined to that body by the power of destiny, O ruler of men.

14.32.s:
viśeṣānnāyakatvaṃ ca gātrebhyaḥ samajāyata ..
bālakapratimaṃ kāntaṃ sarvalakṣaṇalakṣitam .. 9 ..
14.32.d:
विशेषान्नायकत्वं च गात्रेभ्यः समजायत ..
बालकप्रतिमं कान्तं सर्वलक्षणलक्षितम् .. 9 ..
14.32.m: And preeminence arose especially from those limbs; / he looked like a boy, lovely, endowed with all auspicious marks,

14.32.s:
trigaṃbhīraṃ caturhastaṃ saptaraktaṃ mahīpate ..
ṣaḍunnataṃ pañcadīrghaṃ paścasūkṣmaṃ susundaram.. 7.3.32.10 ..
14.32.d:
त्रिगंभीरं चतुर्हस्तं सप्तरक्तं महीपते ..
षडुन्नतं पञ्चदीर्घं पश्चसूक्ष्मं सुसुन्दरम्.. 7.3.32.10 ..
14.32.m: with three deep, four hands, seven red, O king, / six elevated, five long, five subtle, exceedingly beautiful,

14.32.s:
trivistīrṇaṃ mahārāja dṛṣṭvā gaurī suvismitā ..
sajīvaṃ kārayāmāsa svaśaktyā śaktirūpiṇī .. 11 ..
14.32.d:
त्रिविस्तीर्णं महाराज दृष्ट्वा गौरी सुविस्मिता ..
सजीवं कारयामास स्वशक्त्या शक्तिरूपिणी .. 11 ..
14.32.m: and three expansive, O great king. Seeing him, Gaurī was utterly astonished; / she, the embodiment of power, brought him to life by her own power.

14.32.s:
sa sajīvaḥ kṛto devyā samuttasthau ca tatkṣaṇāt ..
ādeśaṃ yācayāmāsa vinayānatakandharaḥ .. 12 ..
14.32.d:
स सजीवः कृतो देव्या समुत्तस्थौ च तत्क्षणात् ..
आदेशं याचयामास विनयानतकन्धरः .. 12 ..
14.32.m: Brought to life by the goddess, he stood up that very instant / and requested a command, bending his neck in modesty.

14.32.s:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā cādbhutākāraṃ proktvā putraṃ muhurmuhuḥ ..
śaṃbhoḥ sakāśamanayatprahṛṣṭenāntarātmanā .. 13 ..
14.32.d:
तं दृष्ट्वा चाद्भुताकारं प्रोक्त्वा पुत्रं मुहुर्मुहुः ..
शंभोः सकाशमनयत्प्रहृष्टेनान्तरात्मना .. 13 ..
14.32.m: Seeing him of wondrous form, calling him her son again and again, / she brought him before Śambhu with a heart overflowing with joy.

14.32.s:
tato'bravītsutaṃ deva mamaiva gātralepajam ..
dehi deva varānitthaṃ mahattvaṃ yena gacchati .. 14 ..
14.32.d:
ततोऽब्रवीत्सुतं देव ममैव गात्रलेपजम् ..
देहि देव वरानित्थं महत्त्वं येन गच्छति .. 14 ..
14.32.m: Then she said, “O God, to my son, born from the paste of my own body, / give boons, O God, so that he may attain greatness.”

14.32.s:
.. śrībhagavānuvāca .. ..
śarīrasthaṃ śiro mukhyaṃ yasmātparvatanandini ..
mahattvidaṃ śiraḥ proktaṃ tvayā skandena yojitam.. 15 ..
14.32.d:
.. श्रीभगवानुवाच .. ..
शरीरस्थं शिरो मुख्यं यस्मात्पर्वतनन्दिनि ..
महत्त्विदं शिरः प्रोक्तं त्वया स्कन्देन योजितम्.. 15 ..
14.32.m: The Lord said: / “Because the head on the body is principal, O daughter of the mountain, / and this head you Skanda joined is said to be huge (mahat),

14.32.s:
viśeṣānnāyakatvaṃ ca gātre cāsya yataḥ sthitam..
mahāvināyako hyeṣa tasmānnāmnā bhaviṣyati .. 16..
14.32.d:
विशेषान्नायकत्वं च गात्रे चास्य यतः स्थितम्..
महाविनायको ह्येष तस्मान्नाम्ना भविष्यति .. 16..
14.32.m: and because preeminence (nāyakatva) resides particularly in his body, / therefore he shall be named Mahāvināyaka.

14.32.s:
gaṇānāṃ caiva sarveṣāmādhipatyaṃ nagātmaje ..
asya dattaṃ mayā yasmādbhaviṣyati gaṇādhipaḥ .. 17 ..
14.32.d:
गणानां चैव सर्वेषामाधिपत्यं नगात्मजे ..
अस्य दत्तं मया यस्माद्भविष्यति गणाधिपः .. 17 ..
14.32.m: Moreover, lordship over all the attendants (gaṇas), O daughter of the mountain, / has been given to him by me, wherefore he shall be the Lord of Attendants (Gaṇādhipa).

14.32.s:
sarvakāryeṣu ye martyāḥ pūrvamenaṃ gaṇādhipam ..
smariṣyaṃti na vai teṣāṃ kāryahānirbhaviṣyati .. 18 ..
14.32.d:
सर्वकार्येषु ये मर्त्याः पूर्वमेनं गणाधिपम् ..
स्मरिष्यंति न वै तेषां कार्यहानिर्भविष्यति .. 18 ..
14.32.m: Those mortals who remember this Gaṇādhipa first in all undertakings / shall never suffer failure in their deeds.”

14.32.s:
tato'sya pradadau skandaḥ prakrīḍārthaṃ kuṭhārakam ..
tadeva cāyudhaṃ tasya supriyaṃ hi sadā'bhavat .. 19 ..
14.32.d:
ततोऽस्य प्रददौ स्कन्दः प्रक्रीडार्थं कुठारकम् ..
तदेव चायुधं तस्य सुप्रियं हि सदाऽभवत् .. 19 ..
14.32.m: Then Skanda gave him an axe to play with, / and that very weapon was indeed always exceedingly dear to him.

14.32.s:
tato gaurī dadau bhojyapātraṃ modakapūritam ..
putrasnehātsa tatprāpya lāsyamevaṃ tadā'karot .. 7.3.32.20 ..
14.32.d:
ततो गौरी ददौ भोज्यपात्रं मोदकपूरितम् ..
पुत्रस्नेहात्स तत्प्राप्य लास्यमेवं तदाऽकरोत् .. 7.3.32.20 ..
